text.en: Orthogonal polynomials and mesh basis functions A mesh supplies cells, geometry and connectivity. A basis supplies the functions used to represent a field on those cells. The choice of basis is separate from cell shape and variable staggering. The basis notebook makes modes, nodes and their mass matrices visible. The existing DG advection example already uses Legendre modes internally; this chapter exposes the algebra behind it. Start on a reference element# Map a physical interval of length h and center x_c to a reference interval: x=xc+Jξ,J=h/2,−1≤ξ≤1,uh(x)=∑j=0pajϕj(ξ). The p+1 coefficients are element degrees of freedom. In a continuous finite-element method, neighboring elements share selected boundary degrees of freedom. DG keeps independent element coefficients and couples traces through numerical fluxes. A local polynomial basis can serve either formulation. For constant material coefficients and an affine map, the element mass and diffusion matrices are Mij=J∫−11ϕiϕj dξ,Kij=J−1∫−11ϕi′ϕj′ dξ. Curved maps introduce a variable Jacobian; variable density or coefficients also change these integrals. Reference-element orthogonality alone then does not make the physical matrix diagonal. Legendre modes and orthonormal modes# With unit weight on [-1,1], the Legendre family satisfies P0=1,P1=ξ,P2=(3ξ2−1)/2,(n+1)Pn+1=(2n+1)ξPn−nPn−1, ∫−11PiPj dξ=22i+1δij,P^i=2i+12Pi. The ordinary Legendre mass is diagonal, with unequal diagonal entries. The orthonormal reference mass is the identity. Their coefficient values differ, although both span exactly the same degree-p polynomial space. The constant mode encodes the element mean; the higher Legendre modes have zero mean. See NIST DLMF §18.3 for normalization and §18.9 for recurrence relations. Nodal Lagrange functions represent the same space# Choose distinct nodes and define cardinal polynomials: ℓj(ξ)=∏k≠jξ−ξkξj−ξk,ℓj(ξi)=δij,uh=∑jujℓj. Here the coefficients u_j are nodal values. In a modal expansion, the coefficients are polynomial amplitudes. For the same polynomial, the change of representation is ui=∑jVijaj,Vij=Pj(ξi),a=V−1u. The notebook compares equispaced nodes and Gauss–Lobatto–Legendre (GLL) nodes. It reports the condition number of this Legendre Vandermonde; that number depends on normalization and is not the condition number of a complete PDE solve. Endpoint clustering can help interpolation, but does not remove Gibbs oscillations at a jump. Quadrature and the diagonal-mass caveat# With p+1 points, Gauss–Legendre quadrature integrates polynomials through degree 2p+1. GLL includes the endpoints and integrates through degree 2p−1. Its interior points are the zeros of P'_p, and its weights are wi=2p(p+1)Pp(ξi)2,p≥1. Products of degree-p basis functions can have degree 2p. Consequently, GLL collocation gives a quadrature mass diag(w), while the exactly integrated GLL nodal mass generally has off-diagonal entries. On an affine interval with unit weight, their difference is rank one. The highest Legendre squared norm is 2/p under GLL quadrature, instead of 2/(2p+1). The notebook lets you switch between both matrices. These facts, and an efficient correction, are derived in Teukolsky's mass-matrix note. For constant-coefficient stiffness, the polynomial degree is at most 2p−2, so the same GLL rule is sufficient. Nonlinear fluxes and variable metrics can require additional quadrature or a suitable split formulation; a diagonal mass alone is not a nonlinear stability guarantee. DLMF §3.5 explains Gaussian quadrature more generally. Projection is different from interpolation# An unweighted L2 Legendre projection uses integral moments: ak=2k+12∫−11f(ξ)Pk(ξ) dξ. Nodal interpolation instead matches f at the chosen nodes. They agree for every polynomial of degree at most p, but need not agree for other functions. For exp(ξ), the notebook shows rapidly decreasing errors as p increases. For sign(ξ), the displayed overshoot and slow convergence expose the loss of smoothness; neither approximation supplies a shock limiter. The jump is integrated on two separate half-intervals, and interpolation explicitly uses sign(0)=0. L2 errors are integrated with 80-point Gauss rules on each half. Quadrilaterals and triangles have different polynomial spaces# On a quadrilateral, a tensor basis takes products of one-dimensional functions: ϕij(ξ,η)=ℓi(ξ)ℓj(η),0≤i,j≤p. This Q_p space has (p+1)^2 functions. A triangle's total-degree P_p space has (p+1)(p+2)/2. Thus Q2 has nine degrees of freedom, while triangular P2 has six. The cell topology determines which reference map and trace connectivity are needed. DefElement's Lagrange definition distinguishes these spaces and nodal variants. On the reference triangle (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), barycentric coordinates are λ0=1−ξ−η, λ1=ξ, λ2=η. The P1 vertex functions are λ_i. P2 has vertex functions λ_i(2λ_i−1) and edge functions 4λ_iλ_j. They form a partition of unity and reproduce quadratic fields; they are not an orthogonal basis. The notebook colors each of these six shape functions on the actual triangle. Orthogonal modal triangle bases can instead be built from suitably weighted Jacobi polynomials in collapsed coordinates, including the Dubiner (1991) construction. A rectangular Legendre tensor product restricted to a triangle does not automatically retain orthogonality. This edition implements P1/P2 nodal triangles and quadrilateral tensor evaluation; a Dubiner implementation remains additional work. Other orthogonal families and their measures# Orthogonality always includes a domain and a weight. Changing either changes the inner product. The notebook also tabulates Chebyshev T modes and demonstrates their nonorthogonality under unit weight. The remaining families below are mathematical reading connections. Conventions follow DLMF §18.2 and §18.3. Chebyshev T_n: T_n(cos θ)=cos(nθ), on [-1,1], weight (1−ξ²)^−1/2. Useful for endpoint-clustered spectral interpolation. They are not mutually orthogonal under the unweighted finite-element mass integral. Jacobi: P_n^(α,β), weight (1−ξ)^α(1+ξ)^β on [-1,1], α,β>−1. This family includes Legendre and, after normalization, Chebyshev; weighted coordinate transforms connect it to simplex bases. Hermite: physicists' H_n has weight exp(−ξ²) on the real line; probabilists' He_n uses exp(−ξ²/2). These are different conventions. Orthogonal Hermite polynomials are distinct from the endpoint value/derivative Hermite interpolation used by CIP. Generalized Laguerre: L_n^(α) uses ξ^α exp(−ξ) on [0,∞), α>−1. It addresses a semi-infinite domain rather than an ordinary bounded mesh cell. Fourier modes: exp(ikx) are orthogonal on a periodic interval with matching integer wave numbers. They form a global periodic basis rather than a mesh-local polynomial family; the spectral advection example uses these modes. Verification and scope# numart.basis supplies Legendre/Chebyshev and nodal tabulation, derivatives, affine interval matrices, GLL quadrature, projection, P1/P2 triangles and tensor products. Tests check continuous Legendre orthogonality, GLL exactness limits, cardinal interpolation, polynomial reproduction, partition of unity, derivative reproduction, the GLL summation-by-parts identity, rank-one mass difference and physical Jacobian scaling. The existing DG solver remains restricted to scalar periodic P0/P1/P2 advection. The published reference-element source is available from the Legendre method record. Saved arrays and source hashes accompany the figure. This adds reference-element building blocks, not a general curved-mesh assembly or a higher-order fluid solver. Continue with mesh connectivity, continuous triangular FEM, DG advection, limiters and variable staggering. text.ja: 解説章公開コード・データ / Public code and data 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。 テスト計算ライブラリ 1次元の各Problemは、方程式、領域、終了時刻、境界、初期条件、参照解、引用キーを保持します。get_problem(name)により、すべての手法から同じ定義を使えます。配列の最後の軸が変数で、Eulerは(ρ,ρu,E)、浅水流は(h,hu)、等温流は(ρ,ρu)です。 滑らかな問題# 線形移流は周期区間[0,1]、速度a、初期値sin(2πx)を使います。厳密な平行移動解と差分・DG・Fourier法を比較します。DGはモード型Legendre P0／P1／P2、風上境界流束、SSPRK3です。Ppの空間次数と時間3次積分を区別してください。DGの未知数は要素数×(p+1)です。Fourier法は線形モードを時間方向に厳密に積分し、このギャラリーから同一コストや同一自由度での順位は導きません。非線形積、エイリアシング除去、Gibbs現象の処理は今後の課題です。 entropy-waveはEulerのρ=1+0.2sin(2πx)、u=1,p=1,γ=1.4、周期区間[0,1]、t=1を使います。密度だけが移動する厳密解で、滑らかな解の精度と周期保存性を検証できます。等温Eulerには独立したエネルギー・エントロピー変数がないため、同じEulerエントロピー波問題は使えません。 衝撃波管# Sod：[0,1]、x0=0.5、左(ρ,u,p)=(1,0,1)、右(0.125,0,0.1)、γ=1.4、t=0.2です。境界はゼロ勾配外挿で、主要な波は終了時刻までに境界へ達しません。厳密リーマンソルバーは二分法で整合する圧力を求め、衝撃波、接触波、膨張波を標本化します。真空を含む厳密解には対応していません。Sod（1978）、厳密解実装の参照先。 Lax：[-5,5]、x0=0、左(0.445,0.698,3.528)、右(0.5,0,0.571)、γ=1.4、t=1.3、外挿境界です。LaxテストとLax–Friedrichs法は、同じ人名でも別の対象です。後の文献で使われる標準的なパラメータを採用し、1954年原論文の表との直接照合はしていません。 Shu–Osher：[-5,5]、x0=-4、t=1.8、γ=1.4、左(3.857143,2.629369,10.33333)、右(1+0.2sin(5x),0,1)です。仮想セルは領域端で評価した初期状態に固定します。終了時刻の厳密参照解はなく、初版の図はMUSCLとWENOの数値結果を比較します。Shu–Osher（1989）、Quokkaの採用パラメータ §3.1.5。 低密度とEinfeldt型のテスト# double-rarefactionは[0,1]、x0=0.5、左(1,-2,0.4)、右(1,2,0.4)、γ=1.4、t=0.15です。強い膨張を起こすこの設定は1–2–3問題とも呼ばれます。選定した正値性テストでは区分一定再構成とHLLEを使います。この保証が高次MUSCLやWENOに移るわけではありません。Einfeldtら（1991）。 浅水流と等温流# dam-breakは平坦底面の浅水流で、g=1、左h=2、右h=1、u=0、[0,1]、t=0.1です。乾燥床、地形ソース、静水平衡を保つ離散化、濡れ・乾きの処理は未対応です。isothermalはp=cs²ρ、cs=1、左ρ=1、右ρ=0.125、u=0を同じ領域・時間区間で解きます。いずれも外挿境界です。初版ではソルバー、許容状態、保存形を検査します。参照解ライブラリに半解析Riemann状態と保存変数セル平均を追加し、方程式ギャラリーで使います。この2ケースの元のProblem.referenceは未設定のままです。新しい評価にはget_referenceを使ってください。LeVeque（2002）。 リーマン流束と再構成# RusanovとHLLはEuler・浅水・等温流に対応します。HLLC、Roe、HLLEは現在、理想気体Eulerだけに対応します。HLLは局所音響速度の最小・最大、HLLEはRoe平均を含むEinfeldt型推定を使います。Roeは音響固有値にδ=0.1ãの2次エントロピー平滑化を適用し、接触固有値は変更しません。低密度の正値性修正や、一般的なエントロピー安定流束の構成とは別です。 MUSCLは基本変数についてminmod（既定）、Superbee、MC、van Leer、切り詰めたvan Albadaを選べます。勾配制限を参照してください。WENO5-JSは点値流束と大域LF分割を使う、成分別の有限差分実装です。後述の別章に特性再構成・WENO-Zを追加し、この従来ソルバーは変更していません。完全離散の正値性保存は今後の課題です。別の発展的な勾配制限ではTVB修正minmodとEulerの正値再構成スケーリングを実装していますが、これらのEuler時間更新とは結合していません。 誤差はpointwiseと表示します。有限体積セル平均と差分点値は厳密には交換できません。Orszag–Tangの定義と限界はMHD、拡散・Poisson問題は楕円型問題を参照してください。 テスト問題と手法を対応させる# 原型KEEPの展示では滑らかな等エントロピー渦と保存量診断を使います。素の中心流束には衝撃波安定化がなく、Sod／DMRソルバーとはしていません。動画ガイドでは、滑らかな流れ、衝撃波捕獲、MHDの計算を区別し、定常場は静止図で示します。 方程式から始めるスカラー比較# 方程式ギャラリーでは、厳密なセル積分を持つBurgers・LWR交通流のリーマン問題、移流・熱拡散モードを加えています。既存のSod、水深が正のダム崩壊、等温流の基準計算にもつなぎ、参照解の規約を明示します。 再構成・流束テストの拡充# 新しい再構成章と操作できる比較に、制限付き放物線FV・保存特性変数・FD WENO-Z・変種を明示したAUSM系列基準例を追加しました。上記の従来コードは成分ごとの基準例として残します。平面衝撃波の感度とRoeのProperty Uは別に検証します。 歴史アトラス →計算結果のギャラリー →
text.en: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Benchmark library For the representation behind DG and spectral examples, see orthogonal polynomials and element bases: Legendre modes, nodal transforms, quadrature, and their mass matrices. Each 1D Problem stores the equation, domain, final time, boundaries, initial condition, reference solution, and citation keys. get_problem(name) exposes the same definition to every method. The last array axis contains variables: Euler uses (ρ,ρu,E), shallow water uses (h,hu), and isothermal flow uses (ρ,ρu). Smooth problems# Linear advection uses periodic [0,1], speed a, and initial data sin(2πx). The exact translated solution compares finite differences, DG, and Fourier methods. DG uses modal Legendre P0/P1/P2, upwind boundary fluxes, and SSPRK3. Distinguish the spatial order of Pp from the third-order time integrator. DG has elements × (p+1) unknowns. Fourier integrates the linear modes exactly in time; the gallery does not establish an equal-cost or equal-degree-of-freedom ranking. Nonlinear products, dealiasing, and Gibbs treatments are future work. entropy-wave uses Euler data ρ=1+0.2sin(2πx), u=1,p=1,γ=1.4, periodic [0,1], and t=1. Only density translates, giving an exact reference for smooth accuracy and periodic conservation. Isothermal Euler has no independent energy or entropy variable and does not support this same Euler entropy-wave problem. Shock tubes# Sod: [0,1], x0=0.5, left (ρ,u,p)=(1,0,1), right (0.125,0,0.1), γ=1.4, and t=0.2. Boundaries use zero-gradient extrapolation; the main waves do not reach them before the final time. The exact Riemann solver finds the matching pressure by bisection and samples shocks, contacts, and rarefaction fans. Exact solutions containing a vacuum are unsupported. Sod (1978), exact-solution implementation reference. Lax: [-5,5], x0=0, left (0.445,0.698,3.528), right (0.5,0,0.571), γ=1.4, t=1.3, and extrapolation boundaries. The Lax test and the Lax–Friedrichs algorithm are different namesakes. These are standard parameters from later literature; the original 1954 paper's table has not been directly matched here. Shu–Osher: [-5,5], x0=-4, t=1.8, γ=1.4, left (3.857143,2.629369,10.33333), and right (1+0.2sin(5x),0,1). Ghost states are fixed to the initial conditions evaluated at the domain ends. There is no exact final-time reference; the first-edition figure compares MUSCL and WENO numerical results. Shu–Osher (1989), adopted parameters in Quokka, §3.1.5. Low densities and Einfeldt-type tests# double-rarefaction uses [0,1], x0=0.5, left (1,-2,0.4), right (1,2,0.4), γ=1.4, and t=0.15. This strong expansion is commonly called the 1–2–3 problem. The selected positivity test uses piecewise-constant reconstruction with HLLE. It does not transfer a positivity guarantee to high-order MUSCL or WENO. Einfeldt et al. (1991). Shallow-water and isothermal flow# dam-break solves flat-bottom shallow water with g=1, left h=2, right h=1, u=0, [0,1], and t=0.1. Dry beds, topographic sources, well-balanced discretization, and wetting/drying are unsupported. isothermal uses p=cs²ρ, cs=1, left ρ=1, right ρ=0.125, and u=0 on the same domain and time interval. Both use extrapolation boundaries. First-edition checks compare solvers, admissible states, and conservative form. The reference library now supplies semi-analytic Riemann states and conserved cell means for the equation gallery. The original Problem.reference callbacks for these two cases remain unset; use get_reference for the new evaluations. LeVeque (2002). Riemann fluxes and reconstruction# Rusanov and HLL support Euler, shallow water, and isothermal flow. HLLC, Roe, and HLLE currently support ideal-gas Euler only. HLL uses minimum/maximum local acoustic speeds; HLLE uses Einfeldt-type estimates including Roe averages. Roe applies quadratic entropy smoothing to acoustic eigenvalues with δ=0.1ã, leaving the contact eigenvalue unchanged. This is neither a low-density positivity fix nor a general entropy-stable flux construction. MUSCL uses selectable minmod (default), Superbee, MC, van Leer, or clipped van Albada reconstruction in primitive variables; see limiters. WENO5-JS is a componentwise finite-difference implementation with pointwise fluxes and global LF splitting. A separate reconstruction chapter below adds characteristics and WENO-Z; this original solver remains unchanged. Fully discrete positivity preservation is still future work. A separate advanced limiter exhibit implements TVB modified minmod and positive Euler reconstruction scaling; neither is coupled to these Euler time updates. Errors are labeled pointwise: finite-volume cell averages and finite-difference point values are not strictly interchangeable. See MHD for Orszag–Tang definitions and limits, and elliptic problems for diffusion and Poisson cases. Matching the benchmark to the scheme# The original KEEP exhibit uses a smooth isentropic vortex and conservation diagnostics. Its bare central flux has no shock stabilization and is not presented as a Sod/DMR solver. The movie guide separates those smooth computations from shock-capturing and MHD movies, and keeps steady fields as still images. Equation-first scalar comparisons# The equation gallery adds Burgers and LWR traffic Riemann problems with exact cell-integrated references, plus advection and heat mode tests. It also connects the existing Sod, wet dam-break and isothermal baselines, with each reference convention explicitly labeled. Expanded reconstruction and flux tests# The new reconstruction chapter and interactive comparison add limited parabolic FV, conservative characteristics, FD WENO-Z and an explicit AUSM-family baseline. The original code described above remains a componentwise baseline. Planar shock sensitivity and Roe's Property U have separate verification. Historical atlas →Computed gallery →

name.ja: SWASHES地形流：静水と非零流量の定常解
name.en: SWASHES topographic flow: lakes and nonzero steady discharge

note.ja: 水没・露出した隆起上の静水と、非零流量の亜臨界定常解を別々に検査します。静水の保存と、動く定常流に残る離散化誤差を区別します。
note.en: Check two lake equilibria separately from nonzero subcritical flow, distinguishing lake preservation from moving-flow discretization error.

name.ja: 乾いた河床のダム破壊：実際のwetting/drying
name.en: Dry-bed dam break: actual wetting and dry states

note.en: Start the right half at exactly h=q=0 and compare wetting-front advance, conservation and conservative errors with the Ritter analytic solution.

note.en: Method-specific editions and related sources; fixed-input runs are listed separately.

name.en: Shu–Osher: independent reference and mesh refinement

note.en: Compare shock–density-wave interaction against separately executed Athena++ reference data rather than a finer grid of the same Python code.

name.ja: Euler二重膨張波：段階ごとの正値性
name.en: Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage

note.ja: 既存の強い二重希薄波を128/256/512セルで計算し、平均保存型の正値性スケーリングをMUSCL・大域LF流束・SSPRK(3,3)へ接続します。各前進Euler段と各SSP凸結合の密度・圧力・境界保存収支を記録します。
note.en: Evolve the existing strong double rarefaction on 128/256/512 cells, connecting mean-preserving positivity scaling to MUSCL, global LF fluxes and SSPRK(3,3). Log density, pressure and boundary budgets for every FE substep and SSP convex combination.

name.ja: 低Mach等エントロピー渦：前処理Roe流束の軽量検証
name.en: Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification

note.ja: 同じ非線形2次元Euler渦をN=16/32/64、背景Mach数.1/.01でT=.1まで進め、通常RoeとMiczek型の空間流束前処理を比較します。全12計算で、速度・動圧スケールの圧力誤差、保存収支、音響刻み、実段状態を調べます。
note.en: The same nonlinear 2D Euler vortex is evolved to T=0.1 on N=16/32/64 at background Mach 0.1/0.01, comparing ordinary Roe with Miczek spatial flux preconditioning. Twelve fixed runs retain velocity and dynamically scaled pressure errors, conserved budgets, acoustic steps and actual stage states.

name.ja: 後期Orszag–Tang：独立参照と圧縮構造
name.en: Late Orszag-Tang: independent reference and compression structure

note.ja: 圧縮性理想MHDのOrszag–TangをT=.2まで進め、相互作用する圧縮・衝撃波構造の密度と圧力を独立有限格子参照で検査します。
note.en: Evolve compressible ideal-MHD Orszag-Tang to T.2 and check density/pressure in interacting compression/shock structure against an independent finite-grid reference.

name.ja: Brio–Wu：HLLDと保存的に粗視化した数値参照
name.en: Brio–Wu: HLLD and a conservatively restricted numerical reference

note.ja: γ=2、Bx=0.75の1次元理想MHD衝撃波管をt=0.1まで計算。HLLD＋MC＋SSPRK2の64/128セルを512セルの数値参照と比較し、密度・圧力・縦磁場・保存収支・切替回数を記録する。
note.en: Evolve the one-dimensional γ=2 ideal-MHD shock tube with Bx=0.75 to t=0.1. Compare 64/128-cell HLLD/MC/SSPRK2 with a 512-cell numerical reference, recording density, pressure, longitudinal field, balances and fallback counts.

name.ja: 円偏波Alfvén波：全成分の格子収束
name.en: Circular Alfven wave: full-state refinement

note.ja: 全8保存変数を進め、非零のBz・vzを含む円偏波を解析セル平均と比較します。
note.en: Evolve all eight conserved variables and compare circular polarization, including nonzero Bz/vz, against analytic cell means.

name.ja: 磁場ループ：独立2次元参照と細分化
name.en: Magnetic loop: independent 2D reference and refinement

note.ja: 実際の2次元磁場ループ輸送を、別実装Athena++の空間・時間感度を検査した終端保存場と比較します。
note.en: Compare genuine 2D magnetic-loop transport with final conserved fields from independent Athena++, qualified in space and time.

name.ja: Noh衝撃波：初期圧力ゼロの平面・円筒・球対称計算
name.en: Noh shocks: zero-pressure planar, cylindrical and spherical flow

note.ja: 初期圧力ゼロのNoh問題を、独自の小型1D有限体積コードで平面・円筒・球対称に計算します。64/128/256/512格子の全域誤差、原点過熱、衝撃位置、保存収支を測り、球で現れる境界流入の時間積分誤差を解析式と照合します。
note.en: An original small 1D finite-volume code solves zero-pressure Noh flow in planar, cylindrical and spherical symmetry. Grids 64/128/256/512 measure full-domain error, origin heating, shock location and budgets, and compare spherical boundary-inflow time-quadrature error with its analytic identity.

name.ja: Zalesak型2D回転輸送：保存・有界性・形状誤差

text.ja: 解説章公開コード・データ / Public code and data 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。 生物モデル方程式と数値検証 小さなモデルから実行・検証する 22モデル族の文献解説に、ロジスティック増殖・閉鎖SIR、線形反応拡散、Schnakenbergの線形発現・有限振幅の非線形発展・成長後の1次元パターン、空間なしFitzHugh–Nagumoの限定例を接続します。全22族の実装ではありません。別配布の固定入力例として、HHの単一細胞電流刺激、移入–死亡SSA、Fisher特殊進行波、2次元Schnakenberg境界モード、強制Keller–Segel製造問題を接続します。 別群small-modelsから、固定した4状態酵素/QSSA、正のLotka–Volterra軌道、SEIR保存則と初期2モード線形化の3例だけを追加します。SEIRはSIRの既存実行範囲とは別です。 反応拡散：空間2次と時間4次を分けて測る Turing不安定性：線形成長率と小振幅パターン FitzHugh–Nagumo：パルス興奮・回復と独立ODE参照 Schnakenberg有限振幅過渡：非線形性と独立参照 Schnakenberg飽和パターン：近定常性と格子・時間収束 同じ非線形反応拡散でLie–TrotterとStrangを比較する 酵素反応の保存と準定常近似 Lotka–Volterra不変量と正値性 SEIR保存則と初期線形化 Hodgkin–Huxley：電位固定・静止平衡・発火 移入–死亡SSA：有限時刻の厳密分布 Fisher–KPP：特殊波速の厳密前線 Schnakenberg：2D境界と初期モード Keller–Segel：連成流束の製造解 ロジスティック・線形反応拡散は解析解、SIR/FHNは別実装DOP853、線形Turingは行列指数です。新しい非線形Schnakenbergは、脱エイリアスしたFourier–Galerkin＋Radauの独立参照と、時間誤差用の同じ差分半離散系のRadau参照を区別します。 追加3ODE例は独立実装のRadau/BDF参照を用い、酵素の縮約モデルは陰的スカラー式、SEIR初期線形化は全2×2行列指数と区別します。 非線形発展・成長後パターンの手法と独立参照を読む · 実装範囲・結果・残る差 個体群の増殖から確率的な遺伝子制御、流体構造連成まで、22の生物・生物由来モデルを選び、保存則CFDの外へ方程式の地図を広げます。22モデル族の文献解説に、ロジスティック増殖・閉鎖SIR、線形反応拡散、Schnakenbergの線形発現・有限振幅の非線形発展・成長後の1次元パターン、空間なしFitzHugh–Nagumoの限定例を接続します。全22族の実装ではありません。別配布の固定入力例として、HHの単一細胞電流刺激、移入–死亡SSA、Fisher特殊進行波、2次元Schnakenberg境界モード、強制Keller–Segel製造問題を接続します。 別群small-modelsから、固定した4状態酵素/QSSA、正のLotka–Volterra軌道、SEIR保存則と初期2モード線形化の3例だけを追加します。SEIRはSIRの既存実行範囲とは別です。 以下は慣用的な簡略形・規格化形です。出典はモデルの系譜を示し、すべての係数や変数が原論文と一致するという意味ではありません。構造化カタログに、各項目の引用、数値的な課題、検証目標、範囲を記録しています。現代数理生物学の網羅的総説ではなく、数値計算の多様性を重視した選定です。出典確認日は2026年11月6日です。 生物の問いと数値計算法の対応# 個体群・生態： ロジスティック増殖、捕食被食、Fisher前線、交差拡散、レプリケータ動力学は、正値性、不変集合、長時間挙動、空間侵入を調べます。 人口構造・感染症： 年齢輸送と区画モデルは、更新境界、収支、区画の非負性、閾値を調べます。 生化学・代謝： 酵素反応とMonod増殖は、硬いODE、保存則、縮約モデルを結びます。 形態形成： Turing解析、Gierer–Meinhardt、Schnakenberg、Gray–Scottでは、物理的な不安定性と数値的な模様選択を分けます。 興奮： Hodgkin–Huxley、FitzHugh–Nagumo、Aliev–Panfilovでは、硬い反応とパルス伝導、不応期、らせん波を結びます。 遺伝子制御・雑音： 遅延フィードバック、トグル、リプレシレーター、化学マスター方程式には、履歴補間、分岐解析、ジャンプ過程のシミュレーションなどが必要です。 生体力学： 流体と弾性構造には、流体方程式に加えて構成力と連成離散化が必要です。 既存の拡散・楕円型解法、有限要素法、疎行列・Newton法、硬い系の時間積分、非圧縮投影法は、その部品になります。既存のテストが、ここで追加した生物系を検証しているわけではありません。 歴史順のモデルカタログ# 年は初期の出典または選んだ発展を指し、排他的な先取権の主張ではありません。後年の空間拡張、縮約、翻訳は各項目で区別します。 01 · 1838 · ロジスティック個体群増殖（Logistic population growth）# ロジスティックの固定入力・解析解比較あり。 環境収容力Kによる密度制限付き増殖です。生物系ODEの最も基本的な比較問題になります。 N˙=rN(1−N/K). 数値的な課題。 正値性、平衡点、Kを越えるオーバーシュートを調べます。滑らかに見える曲線でも不変区間を破る場合があります。 検証案。 N0>0でN(t)=K/[1+(K/N0−1)exp(−rt)]と比較し、時間精度と0、K付近の振る舞いを測ります。 モデルの規約。 リンク先は後年の1847年の論文です。1838年の短報自体は未確認です。この微分方程式は離散ロジスティック写像とは異なります。 出典：Verhulst, Pierre-François (1847)。 02 · 1913 · Michaelis–Mentenと完全酵素反応系（Michaelis–Menten and full enzyme kinetics）# 固定した4状態酵素系とQSSAの限定例。初期層・積分誤差・縮約誤差を区別。 酵素の飽和反応です。質量作用則の全体系は過渡的な複合体Cを解き、縮約速度則は速い変数を消去します。 E+S⇌k−1k1C⟶k2E+P,v=Vmax⁡S/(KM+S). 数値的な課題。 速い初期層と硬さがあり、全体系と縮約系では適用範囲が異なります。通常の準定常近似ではKM=(k−1+k2)/k1です。 検証案。 閉じた反応機構でE+C、S+C+Pの保存を確認します。酵素と基質の尺度比を変え、縮約系と全体系の差を評価します。縮約を厳密解とは扱いません。 モデルの規約。 1913年の迅速平衡の解釈と、1925年の準定常状態による導出を区別します。 出典：Michaelis–Menten（1913、2011年の翻訳を参照）, Briggs, George E. and Haldane, J. (2000)。 動画の前に組み立てる検証経路# 最初の実装順として、ロジスティック／SIR → 酵素反応の全体系 → Fisher前線 → FitzHugh–Nagumoパルス → Schnakenbergモード → Keller–Segel凝集を提案します。捕食被食はHamilton系ノートと並行して長時間不変量を調べ、出生死滅SSAを最初の確率的分岐にできます。Gray–Scottはその後の視覚的な化学展示に向きますが、供給率、空間尺度、初期摂動、出典を明示します。これは実装順の提案で、歴史順とは別です。 非線形前線の厳密解# 尺度化したFisher方程式では、Ablowitz–Zeppetella（1979）の特殊な前線が、決定論的な比較基準になります。 u(x,t)=[1+exp⁡(r6D(x−ct−x0))]−2,c=5Dr6. 有限区間では、厳密解に一致する時間依存境界値を与えるか、境界を十分遠ざけて打ち切りの影響を測ります。前線位置、形状のノルム、時間・空間の細分化をそれぞれ比較します。この特殊な陽表示の前線は最小速度の前線より速く進みます。両者を混同すると、解法に存在しない誤差を検出してしまいます。 模様の発生を定量的に調べる# 選んだ2種反応系の平衡でJacobian Jを作ります。連続体では波数ベクトルkのFourierモードを、次の作用素が発展させます。 L(k)=J−∣k∣2diag⁡(Du,Dv). 一様な正方格子と中心差分Laplacianでは、|k|²を次で置き換えます。 κh2=4h2[sin⁡2(kxh/2)+sin⁡2(kyh/2)]. 小振幅の固有モードをひとつ与え、初期の指数成長を測って、両方の分散関係と比較します。k=0の反応系が安定で非零モードが不安定なら、選んだ拡散駆動不安定性を診断できます。非線形段階の斑点だけでは診断できません。Schnakenbergはこの実験に単純な反応則を与えますが、Turing自身の例と黙って置き換えてはいけません。周期境界とゼロ流束境界では許されるモードが異なります。 解法を評価する前にモデルを固定する# 将来の各計算では、有次元・規格化変数、全パラメータ、初期・境界条件、単位、必要なら乱数種、モデルの版と出典を指定します。収支には境界流束と生成項を含めます。すべての生物反応拡散問題が各種の質量を保存するわけではありません。値を切り詰める正値化は総量や絶滅閾値を変える場合があります。拡散部分を陰的に解くだけでは、分割更新全体の正値性は証明できません。 確率反応網では、離散化・モデル近似と有限標本集団の統計的不確かさを分けます。非線形反応網でODE解が確率系の厳密な平均に一致するとは限りません。遅延方程式では履歴関数と補間則を記録します。生化学の縮約では、モデル縮約誤差と積分誤差を別々に測ります。 出典と今後の分岐# Murrayの第3版入門書（2002）は、これらの分野を横断する読書経路になります。PhysiomeのHodgkin–HuxleyワークスペースとAliev–Panfilovの符号化は、実装パラメータを選ぶ前に確認すべきモデルの版の参照先です。独立した検証データではありません。 今後の独立した調査対象には、神経集団場、空間確率反応拡散、細胞内極性と質量保存反応網、細胞周期のサイズ構造、頂点・位相場による細胞力学、腫瘍と栄養の自由境界、遺伝的浮動を含む集団遺伝学などがあります。現在の22項目が生物モデルの全範囲を尽くすという主張ではありません。指定した方程式に対する数値検証と、生物個体や実験データに対する妥当性検証も異なります。 方程式ギャラリー、歴史アトラス、全参考文献へ戻れます。 歴史アトラス →計算結果のギャラリー →
text.en: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Biological model equations and numerical verification Run and validate small model examples The 22-family survey links scoped examples of logistic growth, closed SIR, linear reaction–diffusion, linear Schnakenberg onset, finite-amplitude nonlinear evolution and post-growth 1D patterns, plus spatially uniform FitzHugh–Nagumo. This does not implement all 22 families. Separate fixed-input releases add single-cell HH current controls, immigration–death SSA, a special Fisher traveling front, 2D Schnakenberg boundary modes and a forced Keller–Segel manufactured problem. Three further fixed examples from the separate small-models group cover four-state enzyme/QSSA, a positive Lotka–Volterra orbit, and SEIR conservation with full two-mode early linearization. SEIR is separate from the existing SIR execution scope. Reaction-diffusion: separate second-order space and fourth-order time Turing instability: linear growth and small-amplitude patterns FitzHugh-Nagumo: pulse excitation, recovery and an independent ODE reference Finite-amplitude Schnakenberg transient: nonlinearity and independent reference Near-saturated Schnakenberg pattern: near-stationarity and grid/time convergence Lie–Trotter versus Strang on the same nonlinear reaction–diffusion input Enzyme conservation and QSSA Lotka–Volterra invariant and positivity SEIR conservation and initial linearization Hodgkin–Huxley: clamps, rest and firing Immigration–death SSA: exact transient laws Fisher–KPP: a special-speed exact front Schnakenberg:2D boundaries and initial modes Keller–Segel: a manufactured coupled-flux solution Analytic references for logistic/linear reaction–diffusion, independent DOP853 for SIR/FHN and matrix exponentials for linear Turing growth. New nonlinear Schnakenberg checks distinguish an independent dealiased Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference from Radau on the same finite-difference semidiscretization used to isolate time error. The three additional ODE examples use separately implemented Radau/BDF references; distinguish the enzyme scalar implicit reduced solution and the full 2×2 exponential used for early SEIR linearization. Read about nonlinear evolution, post-growth patterns and independent references · Implementation scope, results and gaps This survey selects 22 biological and biologically motivated model families, from population growth to stochastic gene regulation and fluid–structure coupling. It expands the equation map beyond conservation-law CFD. The 22-family survey links scoped examples of logistic growth, closed SIR, linear reaction–diffusion, linear Schnakenberg onset, finite-amplitude nonlinear evolution and post-growth 1D patterns, plus spatially uniform FitzHugh–Nagumo. This does not implement all 22 families. Separate fixed-input releases add single-cell HH current controls, immigration–death SSA, a special Fisher traveling front, 2D Schnakenberg boundary modes and a forced Keller–Segel manufactured problem. Three further fixed examples from the separate small-models group cover four-state enzyme/QSSA, a positive Lotka–Volterra orbit, and SEIR conservation with full two-mode early linearization. SEIR is separate from the existing SIR execution scope. The equations below use conventional simplified or normalized forms. A source identifies the model lineage, not a claim that every coefficient and variable matches that paper. The structured catalog retains references, numerical issues, verification targets and scope for each entry. The selection emphasizes numerical variety, rather than a comprehensive review of present-day mathematical biology. Sources checked on 6 November 2026. Which biological questions exercise which algorithms# Population growth and ecology: logistic, predator–prey, Fisher fronts, cross-diffusion and replicator dynamics test positive states, invariant sets, long-time behavior and spatial invasion. Demography and epidemics: age transport and compartment models test renewal boundaries, balances, nonnegative compartments and thresholds. Biochemistry and metabolism: enzyme kinetics and Monod growth connect stiff ODEs, conservation laws and reduced models. Morphogenesis: Turing analysis, Gierer–Meinhardt, Schnakenberg and Gray–Scott separate physical instability from numerical pattern selection. Excitation: Hodgkin–Huxley, FitzHugh–Nagumo and Aliev–Panfilov connect stiff reactions to pulse conduction, refractoriness and spiral waves. Gene regulation and noise: delayed feedback, toggles, repressilators and the chemical master equation need history interpolation, bifurcation analysis or jump-process simulation. Biomechanics: a fluid–elastic structure requires constitutive forces and a coupling discretization in addition to fluid equations. Existing diffusion and elliptic methods, FEM, sparse/Newton methods, stiff integrators and incompressible projection supply useful numerical building blocks. Their current tests do not verify these new biological systems. Historical model catalog# Dates identify an early source or a selected development, not an exclusive priority claim. Later spatial extensions, reductions and translations are identified with their individual entries. 01 · 1838 · Logistic population growth# Logistic fixed-input / analytic checks available. Density-limited growth with carrying capacity K. It is the simplest biological ODE baseline. N˙=rN(1−N/K). Numerical issue. Positivity, preservation of equilibria and overshoot of K; an accurate-looking curve can still violate the invariant interval. Proposed verification. Compare with N(t)=K/[1+(K/N0−1)exp(−rt)] for N0>0; measure temporal order and behavior near 0 and K. Model convention. The linked original is the later 1847 memoir; the 1838 note itself was not audited. The differential equation is not the discrete logistic map. Sources: Verhulst, Pierre-François (1847). 02 · 1913 · Michaelis–Menten and full enzyme kinetics# A fixed four-state enzyme/QSSA example distinguishes initial-layer, integration and reduction errors. Enzyme saturation; the full mass-action system resolves the transient complex C, while the rate law eliminates a fast variable. E+S⇌k−1k1C⟶k2E+P,v=Vmax⁡S/(KM+S). Numerical issue. Fast initial layers and stiffness; full and reduced models have different validity regimes. Under the usual quasi-steady approximation KM=(k−1+k2)/k1. Proposed verification. Check E+C and S+C+P conservation in the closed mechanism. Compare reduced and full systems as enzyme/substrate scales vary, rather than calling the reduction exact. Model convention. The 1913 rapid-equilibrium interpretation and the 1925 quasi-steady-state derivation must remain distinct. Sources: Michaelis–Menten (1913; via the 2011 translation), Briggs, George E. and Haldane, J. B. S. (1925), Johnson, Kenneth A. and Goody, Roger S. (2011). 03 · 1920 · Lotka–Volterra predator–prey# A fixed positive Lotka–Volterra orbit has independent-reference, invariant and step-refinement comparisons. Coupled prey growth and predation; a phase-plane and long-time integration test. x˙=αx−βxy,y˙=δxy−γy. Numerical issue. Positive states and artificial damping or growth of closed orbits. Periodic orbits of this idealized system are not attracting limit cycles. Proposed verification. Monitor H=δx−γ ln(x)+βy−α ln(y) for positive x,y, and compare orbit drift under step refinement. Sources: Lotka, Alfred J. (1920), Volterra, Vito (1926). 04 · 1926 · McKendrick age-structured population# Structured population transport · Survey only. Individuals move through age a at unit speed; newborns enter through a nonlocal renewal boundary. ∂tn+∂an=−μ(a)n,n(0,t)=∫0∞b(a)n(a,t) da. Numerical issue. Upwind/FV transport in age, birth-boundary quadrature and truncation of the infinite age interval. Proposed verification. Use characteristic survival along cohorts and check d∫n da/dt=births−deaths, including any artificial oldest-age outflow. Model convention. This is the classical age-transport form; the later von Foerster lineage is acknowledged without treating its date as the first appearance. Sources: McKendrick, A. G. (1926). 05 · 1927 · SIR and SEIR compartment models# Closed-SIR example retained; SEIR conservation and early linearization have a separate fixed-input example. Closed, well-mixed normalized population fractions. SEIR adds an exposed compartment and a progression rate. s˙=−βsi,i˙=βsi−γi,r˙=γi,s+i+r=1. Numerical issue. Nonnegative compartments, invariant total population and correct resolution of epidemic peak times. Proposed verification. Check total 1 and i+s−(γ/β)ln(s) for β>0,s>0; compare early growth rate βs0−γ and final-size relation in the closed SIR specialization. Model convention. The original general epidemic framework is broader than this SIR specialization. Population-count and fraction conventions give different β definitions. Sources: Kermack, W. O. and McKendrick, A. G. (1927). 06 · 1937 · Fisher–KPP invasion front# Separate fixed-input example: Fisher–KPP: a special-speed exact front. Spatial spread of an invading population or advantageous allele, represented by a reaction–diffusion front. ut=DΔu+ru(1−u),0≤u≤1. Numerical issue. Spatial and temporal front-speed errors; leading-edge resolution, positivity and finite-domain boundary contamination. Proposed verification. Use the Ablowitz–Zeppetella exact front at c=5√(Dr/6), or test the minimal speed 2√(Dr) only with the appropriate steep initial-data regime on a sufficiently large domain. Model convention. Fisher–KPP is a conventional family name; the independent KPP 1937 original remains an archival follow-up. The exact special speed is not the minimal speed. Sources: Fisher, R. A. (1937), Ablowitz, Mark J. and Zeppetella, Anthony (1979). 07 · 1949 · Monod growth and chemostat# Biochemical reactions · Survey only. Nutrient-limited biomass X, substrate S, yield Y and chemostat dilution d; d=0 gives a closed batch model. μ(S)=μmax⁡SKS+S,X˙=(μ(S)−d)X,S˙=d(Sin−S)−μ(S)X/Y. Numerical issue. Washout near a threshold, disparate resource/growth scales, positivity and the distinction between yield and rate constants. Proposed verification. For d=0 check S+X/Y. For d>0 use d(S+X/Y)/dt=d[Sin−(S+X/Y)] and verify the washout equilibrium. Model convention. This writes one constant-yield extension of saturation growth, not a universal metabolic model. Sources: Monod, Jacques (1949). 08 · 1952 · Hodgkin–Huxley membrane dynamics# Separate fixed-input example: Hodgkin–Huxley: clamps, rest and firing. Voltage and gating variables z=m,h,n describe an ionic excitable membrane. A cable extension adds spatial axial current. CmV˙=Iapp−gˉNam3h(V−ENa)−gˉKn4(V−EK)−gL(V−EL),z˙=αz(V)(1−z)−βz(V)z. Numerical issue. Stiff gates, removable singularities in rate formulas, gating bounds, voltage/current sign and temperature conventions. Proposed verification. Select an explicitly versioned CellML/reference convention, verify resting equilibrium and gate relaxation at clamped voltage, then refine spike time and waveform. Model convention. The original squid-axon model is not a calibrated human cardiac model. No single rate parameter set is selected by this survey. Sources: Hodgkin, A. L. and Huxley, A. F. (1952). 09 · 1952 · Turing reaction–diffusion framework# Separate scoped checks of linear onset, nonlinear evolution and post-growth patterns for fixed 1D Schnakenberg systems. A framework for diffusion-driven pattern onset around a homogeneous reaction equilibrium, not a unique choice of f and g. ut=DuΔu+f(u,v),vt=DvΔv+g(u,v). Numerical issue. Physical versus numerical instability, domain eigenmodes and errors in the discrete Laplacian dispersion relation. Proposed verification. For a selected kinetic law compare eigenvalues of J−k²diag(Du,Dv) with early-time Fourier-mode growth. Show that the k=0 reaction equilibrium is stable before asserting diffusion-driven instability. Model convention. A spot image or unequal diffusion coefficients alone do not establish a Turing mechanism. Boundary conditions determine the available modes. Sources: Turing, Alan M. (1952). 10 · 1961 · FitzHugh–Nagumo excitation and recovery# FHN excitation/recovery ODE and time checks retained. Single-cell HH has a separate fixed case; spatial axons and experimental calibration remain unvalidated. A normalized fast excitation/slow recovery model for pulses, refractoriness and spiral waves when extended in space. vt=DΔv+v−v3/3−w+I,wt=ϵ(v+a−bw). Numerical issue. Stiff time-scale separation, splitting error, wave-speed convergence and numerical wave breakup. Proposed verification. Check ODE fixed points/nullclines and small-perturbation eigenvalues first; then refine a 1D pulse before a 2D spiral movie. Model convention. This is a common normalized variant; cubic coefficients, recovery signs and nondimensionalization differ between formulations. Sources: FitzHugh, Richard (1961), Nagumo, Jinichi and Arimoto, Suguru and Yoshizawa, Shuji (1962). 11 · 1970 · Keller–Segel chemotaxis# Separate fixed-input example: Keller–Segel: a manufactured coupled-flux solution. Cell density n drifts up a chemoattractant gradient; τc=0 gives an elliptic chemical subproblem. nt=DnΔn−χ∇⋅(n∇c),τcct=DcΔc+αn−λc. Numerical issue. Cross-coupled flux, positivity, mass conservation and concentrated peaks; spurious undershoots must not be mistaken for physical aggregation or blowup. Proposed verification. With zero total cell flux check ∫n conservation, homogeneous equilibria and linear growth; refine the peak and domain before discussing singularity. Use manufactured smooth solutions before aggregation cases. Model convention. This is a common two-field reduction of a more detailed original formulation. Blowup thresholds depend on dimension, domain, boundary and chemical dynamics. Sources: Keller, Evelyn F. and Segel, Lee A. (1970). 12 · 1972 · Gierer–Meinhardt activator–inhibitor# Pattern formation · Survey only. A representative simplified short-range activation/long-range inhibition model. at=DaΔa+ρa2/h−μa+σa,ht=DhΔh+ρha2−νh. Numerical issue. The inhibitor denominator can become singular; positive h, narrow peaks and reaction stiffness require explicit treatment. Proposed verification. Choose a positive homogeneous equilibrium, check its dispersion relation and inhibitor positivity, then refine spike width and pattern wavelength. Model convention. Source densities, saturation and baseline production vary across the model family. This simplified formula is not a verbatim transcription of every original variant. Sources: Gierer, Alfred and Meinhardt, Hans (1972). 13 · 1972 · Fluid–elastic structure and immersed boundaries# Biomechanics · Survey only. Fluid coupled to a deformable structure; biological examples include valves and membranes, once a force/constitutive law is supplied. ρ(ut+u⋅∇u)=−∇p+μΔu+f,∇⋅u=0,Xt=u(X,t). Numerical issue. Stiff elastic forces, pressure projection, Eulerian–Lagrangian interpolation/spreading and volume leakage. Proposed verification. Specify elastic energy and force before solving. Check force transfer, adjoint interpolation/spreading, fluid divergence and enclosed-volume drift on a simple relaxing boundary. Model convention. Immersed boundary is a numerical coupling method, not itself a closed biological constitutive equation. The existing periodic MAC solver does not implement this coupling. Sources: Peskin, Charles S. (1972). 14 · 1977 · Chemical master equation and Gillespie SSA# Separate fixed-input example: Immigration–death SSA: exact transient laws. Integer molecule counts, reaction jumps νj and propensities aj; SSA samples paths of this continuous-time Markov model. ∂tP(n,t)=∑j[aj(n−νj)P(n−νj,t)−aj(n)P(n,t)]. Numerical issue. Correct combinatorial propensities, event ordering, absorbing states and statistical error; tau-leaping is a separate approximation. Proposed verification. Use immigration–death reactions ∅→X at constant rate k and X→∅ at rate γn: stationary counts are Poisson(k/γ). Compare ensemble mean, variance and distribution with confidence intervals. Model convention. The 1977 paper is a foundational SSA reference, not a priority claim for all master equations. SSA is a solver; the reaction network is the model. A seed documents a trajectory, not an ensemble validation. Sources: Gillespie, Daniel T. (1977). 15 · 1977 · Mackey–Glass delayed physiological feedback# Delay and gene regulation · Survey only. Delayed feedback in a normalized physiological control model; delay can change stability and oscillatory behavior. x˙(t)=βx(t−τ)1+x(t−τ)p−γx(t). Numerical issue. A history function over [−τ,0], delayed interpolation, propagated derivative discontinuities and delay-aware adaptive stepping. Proposed verification. Check the τ=0 ODE limit, a constant equilibrium history and a manufactured forced solution. Compare long-time statistics rather than expecting chaotic trajectories to match pointwise indefinitely. Model convention. A scalar initial value alone is insufficient. The delayed ODE is distinct from a spatial reaction–diffusion model. Sources: Mackey, Michael C. and Glass, Leon (1977). 16 · 1978 · Replicator evolutionary game dynamics# Evolutionary dynamics · Survey only. Strategy fractions reproduce according to relative payoff in a specified matrix game. x˙i=xi[(Ax)i−xTAx],xi≥0,∑ixi=1. Numerical issue. Preserving the probability simplex, behavior near extinction boundaries, neutral cycles versus attracting equilibria. Proposed verification. Check simplex conservation, exact invariant faces and an analytically chosen game equilibrium; use the appropriate game-specific invariant or Lyapunov function. Model convention. No universal Lyapunov function or equivalence of fixed point and evolutionarily stable strategy is assumed. Sources: Taylor, Peter D. and Jonker, Leo B. (1978). 17 · 1979 · Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion# Finite-amplitude nonlinear evolution and post-growth patterns compared with independent references and separate space/time refinement; no general pattern-selection claim. A simple autocatalytic kinetic law extended in space, useful for reproducible Turing-onset tests. ut=DuΔu+a−u+u2v,vt=DvΔv+b−u2v. Numerical issue. Reaction stiffness, positive concentrations and the distinction between kinetic Hopf and spatial Turing instabilities. Proposed verification. Check u*=a+b, v*=b/(a+b)², then compare mode-growth rates with the linearized discrete and continuum operators under fixed boundaries. Model convention. A mathematical chemical pattern model; matching a visual biological pattern does not calibrate it to a tissue. Sources: Schnakenberg, Jürgen (1979). 18 · 1979 · Shigesada–Kawasaki–Teramoto cross-diffusion# Population and ecology · Survey only. Competition with density-dependent self- and cross-dispersal can produce spatial segregation. ut=Δ[(d1+α11u+α12v)u]+u(a1−b1u−c1v),vt=Δ[(d2+α21u+α22v)v]+v(a2−b2u−c2v). Numerical issue. A coupled nonlinear diffusion matrix, loss of simple scalar maximum-principle arguments, positivity and entropy-compatible discretization. Proposed verification. Start with manufactured smooth solutions and constant-state equilibria. With reactions removed and no normal flux, conserve each species mass; check coefficient assumptions before claiming an entropy law. Model convention. The displayed homogeneous-environment reduction omits the original environmental-potential terms. It is not equivalent to two independent scalar diffusion equations. Sources: Shigesada, Nanako and Kawasaki, Kohkichi and Teramoto, Ei (1979). 19 · 1983 · Gray–Scott spatial autocatalysis# Pattern formation · Survey only. A chemical feed/decay model whose spatial extension supports diverse spot and wave patterns. ut=DuΔu−uv2+F(1−u),vt=DvΔv+uv2−(F+k)v. Numerical issue. Sensitivity to F,k, diffusion, domain and finite-amplitude initial perturbations; grid-scale patterns and floating-point variation can affect long-time morphology. Proposed verification. Record every parameter and the perturbation seed. Verify the homogeneous (1,0) state and early perturbation response, then perform grid/time refinement of quantitative observables. Model convention. 1983 is the well-mixed CSTR source; Pearson 1993 is the spatial pattern reference. Spot division does not by itself demonstrate cell division or a linear Turing instability. Sources: Gray, Peter and Scott, Stephen K. (1983), Pearson, John E. (1993). 20 · 1996 · Aliev–Panfilov cardiac excitation# Excitable systems · Survey only. A reduced phenomenological excitation/recovery model for cardiac waves and restitution. ut=DΔu−ku(u−a)(u−1)−uv,vt=(ϵ0+μ1vu+μ2)[−v−ku(u−b−1)]. Numerical issue. Stiff recovery, denominator behavior and sensitivity of wave speed/restitution to resolution and time splitting. Proposed verification. Select a specific model encoding and parameters; establish single-cell and 1D conduction convergence before 2D reentry. Compare a restitution curve, not only a spiral image. Model convention. Monodomain/bidomain tissue models add conductivity tensors and, for bidomain, an extracellular elliptic constraint. They are not automatically included by this two-variable model. Sources: Aliev, R. R. and Panfilov, A. V. (1996). 21 · 2000 · Repressilator mRNA–protein network# Delay and gene regulation · Survey only. Three repressing genes form a cyclic network; retaining mRNA and protein gives six state variables. m˙i=α1+pi−1n+α0−mi,p˙i=β(mi−pi),i=1,2,3 cyclic. Numerical issue. Multiple degradation scales, oscillation onset, phase error and differences between deterministic cycles and noisy individual-cell behavior. Proposed verification. Check the symmetric equilibrium and its linear stability. Compare period and amplitude under time refinement after a stated transient. Model convention. The six-variable form is distinct from a reduced three-protein oscillator; oscillations are parameter-dependent. Sources: Elowitz, Michael B. and Leibler, Stanislas (2000). 22 · 2000 · Genetic toggle switch# Delay and gene regulation · Survey only. Mutual repression produces a possible bistable genetic switch in a normalized model. u˙=α11+vp−u,v˙=α21+uq−v. Numerical issue. Parameter-dependent bistability, saddle separatrices, continuation and sensitivity to perturbations near basin boundaries. Proposed verification. Find all positive equilibria and their Jacobian eigenvalues; verify hysteresis with sufficiently slow continuation and multiple initial conditions. Model convention. Bistability is not guaranteed for arbitrary Hill exponents or production rates. Induction, mRNA dynamics and noise are additional model choices. Sources: Gardner, Timothy S. and Cantor, Charles R. and Collins, James J. (2000). A verification path before attractive movies# A practical first sequence is logistic/SIR → full enzyme kinetics → Fisher front → FitzHugh–Nagumo pulse → Schnakenberg modes → Keller–Segel aggregation. Predator–prey can run alongside the Hamiltonian notebook as a long-time invariant test, while a birth–death SSA provides the first stochastic branch. Gray–Scott is a later visually useful chemical exhibit, with explicit feed rates, spatial scales, initial perturbation and source attribution. This order is an implementation proposal, separate from the historical order. An exact nonlinear front# For the scaled Fisher equation, the special front of Ablowitz–Zeppetella (1979) gives a particularly useful deterministic reference: u(x,t)=[1+exp⁡(r6D(x−ct−x0))]−2,c=5Dr6. A finite interval should use matching time-dependent analytic boundary data, or put boundaries far enough away and quantify the truncation effect. Compare front location, profile norms and temporal/spatial refinement separately. The special explicit front travels faster than the minimal-speed front; confusing these two reference problems would produce a false solver error. Pattern onset is a quantitative test# For a chosen two-species reaction equilibrium, form its Jacobian J. On the continuum, a Fourier mode with wavevector k evolves under L(k)=J−∣k∣2diag⁡(Du,Dv). On a uniform square grid with a centered Laplacian, replace |k|² by κh2=4h2[sin⁡2(kxh/2)+sin⁡2(kyh/2)]. Seed one small eigenmode, measure its early exponential growth and compare both dispersion relations. A stable k=0 reaction system and an unstable nonzero mode diagnose the selected diffusion-driven instability; nonlinear late-time spots alone do not. Schnakenberg supplies a simple kinetic law for this exercise; it should not be silently substituted for Turing's own example. Periodic and zero-flux boundaries admit different mode sets. Preserve the model before judging the method# Each future run should specify dimensional or normalized variables, the full parameter set, boundary/initial conditions, units, random seed where relevant, model version and source. Balances include boundary flux and source terms: not every biological reaction–diffusion problem conserves each species mass. Positivity fixes that clip values may change totals and extinction thresholds. An implicit diffusion step alone does not prove positivity of a split update. For stochastic networks, distinguish discretization/model approximation from finite-ensemble sampling uncertainty. For nonlinear reaction networks the ODE solution need not equal the exact stochastic mean. For delayed equations, record the history function and interpolation rule. For biochemical reductions, measure the model-reduction error separately from integration error. Sources and further branches# Murray's third-edition introduction (2002) provides a broad reading route across these branches. Physiome's Hodgkin–Huxley workspace and Aliev–Panfilov encoding are model-version references to inspect before choosing implementation parameters, rather than independent validation data. Separate follow-up surveys could cover neural population fields, spatial stochastic reaction–diffusion, intracellular polarity and mass-conserving reaction networks, cell-cycle size structure, vertex/phase-field cell mechanics, tumor/nutrient free boundaries, and population genetics with drift. These are additional branches, not a claim that the current 22 entries exhaust biological modeling. Numerical verification against a stated equation is also different from validation against organism- or experiment-specific data. text.ja: Bratu逆問題：合成観測からλを随伴勾配で推定する 順問題を「係数から状態を求める」計算とすれば、逆問題は「観測された状態から係数を推定する」計算です。ここではBratu方程式の5つの観測値から1つのパラメータλを推定し、前章で導いた離散随伴勾配を実際の最適化の更新に使います。対象は、既知の方程式・境界条件・観測位置を持つ小規模な合成問題です。 何を既知とし、何を推定するか 状態u、座標x、係数λは、この教育用モデルでは無次元です。格子、区間[0,1]、ゼロDirichlet境界条件、観測演算子Hと重みWは固定します。未知量はλだけで、モデルの形や境界値を同時に推定する例ではありません。内部未知数nに対する中心差分を使い、各試行λで非線形方程式を解き直します。 −u′′−λeu=0,u(0)=u(1)=0,Fh(u,λ)=Dhu−λeu=0,Dh=h−2tridiag⁡(−1,2,−1),h=(n+1)−1. uα(x)=−2log⁡ ⁣cosh⁡(α(x−1/2))cosh⁡(α/2),λ(α)=2α2cosh⁡2(α/2),α∗=1.5,λ∗≈2.684636137266. 合成データの生成値はα*=1.5、λ*≈2.684636137266です。λ∈[0.2,3.4]に制限し、状態の初期値を毎回ゼロとして、小さい解の枝を対象にします。数値的な枝の選択を問題設定に含めます。折り返し点を越える追跡や高い方の解の枝での推定は検証していません。 観測演算子と重み付き最小二乗 xobs=(1/8,1/4,1/2,3/4,7/8),rh(λ)=Hhuh(λ)−d,W=diag⁡(wj),wj=1/5. 5つのセンサーをx=0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.875に置きます。n=15,31,63,127のいずれでも格子点に一致するため、Hは対応する内部状態を取り出す行列です。この例に補間誤差は入りません。固定されたゼロ端点を観測する行はゼロになります。観測値dは最適化開始前に保存し、各試行λに合わせて生成し直しません。 Φh(λ)=12rh(λ)TWrh(λ)+γ2(λ−λprior)2,γ≥0,ℓ=0.2≤λ≤b=3.4. 公開実験はすべてγ=0、wⱼ=1/5です。そのため目的関数は観測残差の平均二乗の半分です。実装は正の非一様重みと任意のγ≥0も受け取り、別テストで重み・事前値への陽な依存を検査します。Wを観測誤差の逆共分散と解釈するには、別途その確率モデルが必要です。ここではその仮定を置きません。 観測残差から随伴勾配を組み立てる J=Fu=Dh−λdiag⁡(eu),Fλ=−eu,q=HhTWrh,JTp=q. dΦhdλ=γ(λ−λprior)⏟explicit parameter term−pTFλ=γ(λ−λprior)+pTeu. 状態の偏微分qに、Hの転置と観測重みを両方含めます。LagrangianをΦ−pᵀFとする規約では、総微分は陽な項からpᵀF_λを引きます。F_λ=−exp(u)なので、Bratuの状態を通した項はプラスになります。γ=0では陽な項だけがゼロであり、状態を通した項までゼロになるわけではありません。 順問題を収束させた状態でJを組み立て、Jᵀp=qを解きます。既存の陰関数微分の線形求解を使い、Newton反復列を展開して微分しません。このBratuのJは対称です。転置を検査する独立の非対称製造問題は前章の配布版に、観測演算子・非一様重み・正則化の検査は今回の専用テストにあります。 λが1つ、目的関数も1つなので、直接感度Js=exp(u)を解く方法でも右辺は1本です。随伴の計算時間の優位性を示す例ではありません。多数のパラメータへ拡張する際の構成を、小さな逆問題で確認する例です。 箱制約つき勾配法を実際に動かす Π[ℓ,b](z)=min⁡(b,max⁡(ℓ,z)),λtrial=Π[ℓ,b](λk−agk),Δλ=λtrial−λk. Φh(λtrial)≤Φh(λk)+cgkΔλ,c=10−4,a=10 2−j,j=0,1,…. 現在点の随伴勾配gを使ってλを更新し、区間へ射影します。ステップの候補は毎反復a=10から始め、上の十分減少条件を満たすまで半分にします。右辺のgΔλには、射影後の実際の変位を使います。受理・棄却された候補を含め、各評価で同じ非線形求解の制御を使います。順問題が失敗すれば、目的関数の有効な評価として扱わず停止します。 G(λ)=λ−Π[ℓ,b](λ−g(λ)),∣G(λ)∣≤10−10. 停止判定は単位ステップで定義した射影勾配写像の絶対値です。内部最適点では通常の勾配と一致しますが、制約端点ではgがゼロでなくても制約付き停留点となり得ます。最大300更新、線探索は最大50試行で、終了理由・全受理点・ステップ長・後退回数・順問題残差・随伴残差を保存します。目的関数が少し変化しただけでは収束としません。 Armijo（1966）の原論文の十分減少・可変ステップの考え方を参照し、この教材では射影後の変位に適用します。原論文の無制約問題の収束定理を、この非線形逆問題全体の大域収束保証として引用しません。BFGSや汎用の制約付き最適化実装を追加したわけでもありません。 3種類の合成データを混同しない ddisc=Hhuh(λ∗),djcont=uα∗(xj),dnoisy=dcont+10−3(1,−0.6,0.4,−1,0.3)T. 同じ離散化から生成した無雑音データ。 n=31の順問題でdを作り、その同じ離散化を逆問題にも使います。λ*の再現は、データ生成・観測・勾配・最適化が整合することを確かめるinverse crimeです。連続問題や実測データに対する精度の証拠にはしません。 独立した連続解族から生成した無雑音データ。 解析式u_αを観測点で評価して固定します。逆問題の有限差分格子をn=15,31,63,127と細分化すると、生成値との差に含まれる空間離散化の偏りを調べられます。 固定摂動を加えたデータ。 同じ連続解の5成分に、上式の決定論的な摂動を一度だけ加えます。乱数や既知のノイズ分布を仮定せず、摂動の再標本化はしません。固定摂動の公開適合はn=63です。最良適合値が生成λ*からずれても、最適化の失敗とは限りません。 検証：勾配・最適化・格子・観測を分ける 保存した全測定値と入力データから、図・設定・残差・終了理由を確認できます。 gFD(ε)=Φh(λ+ε)−Φh(λ−ε)2ε,Fh(uh(λ±ε),λ±ε)=0. 停留点以外で勾配を照合。 複数のλでλ±εの状態をそれぞれ解き直し、目的関数だけの中心差分と随伴勾配を比較します。最適点付近の両者が単にゼロに近いことだけを検査しません。 独立した1次元参照。 勾配を使わない黄金分割探索と随伴勾配による適合結果を比較します。黄金分割は単峰性を前提とし、標本化した目的関数曲線も保存します。この一致を全分枝での大域最適性の証明にはしません。 3つの初期値。 0.5,1.5,3.2からの更新・目的関数の減少・射影勾配・終了理由を照合します。 生成方法と格子の違い。 同じ離散化での再現性、連続データへの格子誤差、固定摂動による最良適合値の移動を別々に記録します。 保存した実測値①：勾配の照合。 n=31、λ=0.8,1.8,3.0でε=10⁻⁵とした中心差分との差は、順に約1.31×10⁻¹²、2.81×10⁻¹²、1.79×10⁻¹²です。状態感度から作る直接勾配との絶対差は、最大1.4×10⁻¹⁷未満でした。JSONには摂動幅の走査も保存しています。これは実装された離散目的関数の微分の検査です。 実測値②：同じ離散化での回復。 n=31で初期λ=0.5,1.5,3.2から始めると、受理した更新は33,30,25回、生成λ*との絶対差は約1.48×10⁻⁹、1.10×10⁻⁹、1.65×10⁻⁹でした。3例とも射影勾配は10⁻¹⁰以下、観測残差RMSは3.9×10⁻¹⁰未満です。この高い一致は同じ離散化による整合性検査として読みます。 実測値③：連続データへの格子依存。 n=15,31,63,127で推定λは約2.6816989071、2.6839024768、2.6844527616、2.6845902950です。λ*との差の絶対値は約2.9372×10⁻³、7.3366×10⁻⁴、1.8338×10⁻⁴、4.5842×10⁻⁵で、hを半分にするごとにおおむね4分の1になります。観測された次数は2.0013、2.0003、2.0001です。最適化が収束しても、有限格子では生成λ*との差が残ります。 実測値④：固定摂動で最良適合値が移る。 n=63で推定λ≈2.6841620622となり、同じ格子の無摂動データの最適値から約−2.9070×10⁻⁴ずれます。生成λ*との絶対差は約4.7408×10⁻⁴、観測残差RMSは約7.1942×10⁻⁴、目的関数は約2.5878×10⁻⁷です。射影勾配は約6.39×10⁻¹¹なので、真値との差を未収束だけで説明しません。 連続データの4格子と固定摂動の適合は、目的関数だけの黄金分割参照とλで2.1×10⁻⁹以内に一致します。参照探索の最終区間幅は約8.65×10⁻⁹以下で、厳密な最適値の証明ではありません。上記8つの最終適合の順問題残差は1.4×10⁻¹¹以下でした。勾配の照合、最適化の停止、生成値への近さを別々に判定します。 識別できる観測と、できない観測 内部観測がλに反応することは、この1パラメータ問題で局所的な識別を考える手がかりになります。ただし、感度が小さければデータの小さな変化が大きな推定値の変化を生み得ます。局所感度だけで大域的な一意性は示せません。枝・観測位置・許容区間を変えると別の推定問題になります。 反例として端点x=0,1だけを観測すると、Dirichlet値はλによらずゼロなのでH=0、H text.en: Bratu inverse problem: estimate λ from synthetic observations with adjoint gradients A forward problem computes a state from a coefficient; an inverse problem estimates that coefficient from observations of the state. Fit one Bratu parameter λ to five observations and use the previous chapter’s discrete adjoint gradient in the actual optimization updates. The model, boundary conditions and observation positions are known in this small synthetic problem. Specify the known inputs and the unknown parameter State u, coordinate x and coefficient λ are dimensionless in this educational model. The grid, interval [0,1], zero Dirichlet boundary conditions, observation operator H and weights W are fixed. Only λ is unknown; model form and boundary values are not inferred simultaneously. Use centered differences with n interior unknowns and re-solve the nonlinear equation at each trial parameter. −u′′−λeu=0,u(0)=u(1)=0,Fh(u,λ)=Dhu−λeu=0,Dh=h−2tridiag⁡(−1,2,−1),h=(n+1)−1. uα(x)=−2log⁡ ⁣cosh⁡(α(x−1/2))cosh⁡(α/2),λ(α)=2α2cosh⁡2(α/2),α∗=1.5,λ∗≈2.684636137266. The generating values are α*=1.5 and λ*≈2.684636137266. Restrict λ to [0.2,3.4] and start every state solve at zero to target the smaller-solution branch. Numerical branch selection is part of the problem specification. Fitting on the upper branch or continuing through a fold is not verified. Observation operators and weighted least squares xobs=(1/8,1/4,1/2,3/4,7/8),rh(λ)=Hhuh(λ)−d,W=diag⁡(wj),wj=1/5. Five sensors lie at x=0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.875. They coincide with grid nodes for n=15,31,63,127, so H selects interior state entries; no interpolation error is introduced. A row observing a fixed zero endpoint is zero. Save the observations d before optimization and keep them fixed rather than regenerating them for each trial λ. Φh(λ)=12rh(λ)TWrh(λ)+γ2(λ−λprior)2,γ≥0,ℓ=0.2≤λ≤b=3.4. All published experiments use γ=0 and wⱼ=1/5, making the objective half the mean squared observation residual. The implementation also accepts positive nonuniform weights and γ≥0, with separate tests for the weights and explicit prior term. Interpreting W as an inverse error covariance would require a specified probability model; none is assumed here. Build an adjoint gradient from observation residuals J=Fu=Dh−λdiag⁡(eu),Fλ=−eu,q=HhTWrh,JTp=q. dΦhdλ=γ(λ−λprior)⏟explicit parameter term−pTFλ=γ(λ−λprior)+pTeu. The state partial derivative q includes both the transpose of H and the observation weights. With the Lagrangian convention Φ−pᵀF, subtract pᵀF_λ from the explicit parameter derivative. Since F_λ=−exp(u), the Bratu state-mediated term has a plus sign. Setting γ=0 removes the explicit term, not the state-mediated term. Assemble J at the converged primal state and solve Jᵀp=q using the existing implicit-differentiation linear algebra. Do not differentiate an unrolled Newton iteration sequence. This Bratu J is symmetric: an independent nonsymmetric manufactured problem tests transposition in the previous release, while the new dedicated tests check the observation operator, nonuniform weights and regularization. There is one parameter and one objective, so a direct sensitivity solve Js=exp(u) also has one right-hand side. This example demonstrates no adjoint speed advantage. It checks a construction that can extend to many parameters on a small inverse problem. Run a gradient method with box constraints Π[ℓ,b](z)=min⁡(b,max⁡(ℓ,z)),λtrial=Π[ℓ,b](λk−agk),Δλ=λtrial−λk. Φh(λtrial)≤Φh(λk)+cgkΔλ,c=10−4,a=10 2−j,j=0,1,…. Update λ using its current adjoint gradient g and project into the interval. Restart the step length at a=10 on each iteration and halve it until the sufficient-decrease inequality holds. Use the actual displacement after projection in gΔλ. Accepted and rejected trial evaluations use the same primal controls. A failed state solve stops the calculation rather than supplying a valid objective value. G(λ)=λ−Π[ℓ,b](λ−g(λ)),∣G(λ)∣≤10−10. The stopping measure is the absolute projected-gradient mapping with a unit step. It equals the ordinary gradient at an interior solution where projection is inactive; at an active bound a nonzero g can satisfy constrained stationarity. Save every accepted point, step length, backtrack count, primal/adjoint residual and termination reason, with at most 300 updates and 50 line-search trials. A small objective change alone is not the convergence test. Armijo (1966) provides the sufficient-decrease and variable-step idea; this implementation applies it to the projected displacement. The original unconstrained convergence theorem is not cited as a global-convergence guarantee for this nonlinear inverse problem. This is also not an implementation of BFGS or a general constrained-optimization library. Keep three synthetic data regimes distinct ddisc=Hhuh(λ∗),djcont=uα∗(xj),dnoisy=dcont+10−3(1,−0.6,0.4,−1,0.3)T. Noiseless data from the same discretization. Generate d with the n=31 forward solver and invert with that same discretization. Recovering λ* is an inverse crime: it checks consistency among data generation, observations, gradient and optimizer, not accuracy for the continuous problem or real measurements. Noiseless data from the independent continuous family. Fix the closed-form u_α values at the observation points. Refine the inverse grid through n=15,31,63,127 to examine discretization bias in the difference from the generating parameter. Data with a fixed perturbation. Add the displayed deterministic vector once to the same continuous observations. No random draw or known noise distribution is assumed, and no resampling occurs. The published perturbed-data fit uses n=63. A best fit displaced from λ* need not indicate optimizer failure. Verification: gradients, optimization, grids and observations The saved measurements and input data record figure values, controls, residuals and termination reasons. gFD(ε)=Φh(λ+ε)−Φh(λ−ε)2ε,Fh(uh(λ±ε),λ±ε)=0. Check gradients away from stationary points. Re-solve the state at λ±ε for several λ and compare objective-only central differences with adjoint gradients. Do not rely only on both gradients being nearly zero at an optimum. Use an independent scalar reference. Compare the adjoint-gradient fit with objective-only golden-section search. Golden section assumes a unimodal objective; sampled objective landscapes are also saved. Agreement is not a proof of global optimality across all branches. Use three starting values. Compare accepted updates, objective decrease, projected gradients and termination reasons from 0.5,1.5,3.2. Vary the data generation and grid separately. Record same-discretization consistency, mesh error for continuous data and the shift in best fit under the fixed perturbation. Saved measurements 1: gradient checks. At n=31 and λ=0.8,1.8,3.0, central differences with ε=10⁻⁵ differ from adjoint gradients by approximately 1.31×10⁻¹², 2.81×10⁻¹² and 1.79×10⁻¹². The maximum absolute direct-sensitivity/adjoint gradient difference is below 1.4×10⁻¹⁷. The JSON also saves a perturbation sweep. These check derivatives of the implemented discrete objective. Measurements 2: same-discretization recovery. For n=31, starts λ=0.5,1.5,3.2 take 33,30,25 accepted updates. Absolute errors from λ* are approximately 1.48×10⁻⁹, 1.10×10⁻⁹ and 1.65×10⁻⁹. All three projected gradients are at most 10⁻¹⁰ and data RMS residuals below 3.9×10⁻¹⁰. Read this close agreement as a same-discretization consistency check. Measurements 3: mesh dependence for continuous data. For n=15,31,63,127, fitted λ values are approximately 2.6816989071, 2.6839024768, 2.6844527616, 2.6845902950. Absolute errors from λ* are approximately 2.9372×10⁻³, 7.3366×10⁻⁴, 1.8338×10⁻⁴, 4.5842×10⁻⁵, decreasing by about four as h halves. Observed orders are 2.0013, 2.0003, 2.0001. The optimizer converges while finite-mesh bias remains. Measurements 4: a fixed perturbation shifts the best fit. At n=63 the fitted λ≈2.6841620622 shifts by about −2.9070×10⁻⁴ from the unperturbed optimum on the same grid. Absolute error from λ* is about 4.7408×10⁻⁴, data RMS residual about 7.1942×10⁻⁴ and objective about 2.5878×10⁻⁷. The projected gradient is about 6.39×10⁻¹¹, so the departure from truth is not explained simply by unfinished optimization. The four continuous-data fits and the fixed-perturbation fit agree with the objective-only golden-section reference to within 2.1×10⁻⁹ in λ. The reference’s final interval width is below about 8.65×10⁻⁹; it is not a certificate of an exact optimum. Primal residuals at the eight final fits above are at most 1.4×10⁻¹¹. Judge derivative agreement, optimizer stopping and closeness to the generating parameter separately. Observations that can and cannot identify λ Js=eu,d(Hhuh)dλ=Hhs,∥W1/2Hhs∥2>0 is a local sensitivity diagnostic. A response of the interior observations to λ is a useful local sensitivity diagnostic in this scalar problem. A weak response can amplify small data changes into large parameter changes. Local sensitivity alone does not prove global uniqueness. Changing the branch, sensor positions or admissible interval changes the inverse problem. For a counterexample, observe only x=0,1. Their fixed Dirichlet values vanish independently of λ, so H=0 and Hs=0. With γ=0, the objective is independent of λ and the data cannot identify it. Dedicated tests check this property, and the fitting function rejects this setting as uninformative. A regularization term could select a parameter but would not make the boundary observations informative. The fixed-perturbation experiment supplies no statistical confidence intervals. Real observations, unknown model discrepancy, optimal sensor placement and identifiability of many parameters are outside the verified scope. Separate parameter error from optimization error eλ=∣λ^h−λ∗∣,rdata=15∑j=15(Hhuh−d)j2,rF=∥Fh(uh,λ)∥2,rp=∥JTp−q∥2. Error from the generating λ*, observation residual, primal residual, adjoint residual and projected gradient are different quantities. A small projected gradient checks stationarity for the chosen grid, observations and constraints; it does not guarantee truth recovery or a zero observation residual. Conversely, continuous/discrete mismatch or fixed observation perturbations can move a well-converged optimum away from λ*. Primal solves use an unscaled Euclidean residual tolerance of 10⁻¹⁰ and at most 40 updates. Adjoint systems use small dense matrices. Finite-difference gradient checks balance perturbation truncation, roundoff and inner-solve error. Mesh refinement, tighter optimizer stopping and improvement of a physical model address different errors. This release is an educational scalar, box-constrained fit on a specified Bratu branch. It is not a general inverse-problem library, quasi-Newton implementation, transient adjoint, singular-point continuation method, model-selection procedure or validation of a physical model with experimental data. Run the fixed release and inspect its inputs Extract the dated release ZIP and follow the README. The earlier AD and sensitivity supplements remain separate, fixed releases; this synthetic inverse example has its own package. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python scripts/build_bratu_inverse.py python -m pytest tests/test_bratu_inverse.py Inspect the objective, adjoint and optimizer source, figure and evidence builder, dedicated tests, independent-extraction verification record and file inventory and SHA-256 hashes. JSON inputs include positions, generating parameter, fixed perturbation, weights, starts and stopping controls. Blondel et al. (2022), Section 2.1, and the official JAXopt documentation discuss root derivatives built from residual derivatives and linear solves; Jameson (1988) gives historical context for adjoints in design. This NumPy educational implementation does not claim to reproduce their paper experiments or JAXopt’s implementation or performance. Publication scope and related entries An educational box-constrained adjoint-gradient implementation estimates one Bratu coefficient λ from synthetic observations. Measured checks cover same-discretization consistency, mesh dependence for independent continuous-family data, fixed observation perturbations, gradient differences and an objective-only reference search. Scope is a specified smaller-solution branch, fixed observations and small dense matrices. It does not validate BFGS or optimization methods generally, all-branch uniqueness, real data, statistical uncertainty or unknown model discrepancy. text.ja: Bratu逆問題の複数パラメータ化：正則化と識別可能性 係数を1個から2個へ増やすと、観測への適合だけでは判断しにくい問題が現れます。ある組み合わせには観測が強く反応しても、別の組み合わせにはほとんど反応しないことがあるからです。ここでは前章の定数λを位置依存の係数λ(x)へ拡張し、随伴勾配による推定、正則化による選択、観測が持つ情報を分けて検証します。 定数λを、平均と傾きの2係数へ拡張する −u′′(x)−λ(x;θ)eu(x)=0,u(0)=u(1)=0,λ(x;θ)=a+b(2x−1),θ=(a,b)T.
