A standalone Strang step calls one additional subflow. Over consecutive constant steps, adjacent half F steps can be merged when the exact flow has the group property (a positive-time semigroup suffices for diffusion). Lie–Trotter uses 2N subflow calls and merged Strang 2N+1. Actual work depends on each subproblem, output and boundary processing, and whether numerical subflows permit merging. Call counts are not measured runtimes. Small noncommuting example with exact subflows u=(qp),A=(0100),B=(00−10),u(0)=(10),u(t)=(cos⁡t−sin⁡t). φAh(q,p)=(q+hp,p),φBh(q,p)=(q,p−hq),[A,B]=(−1001). Lhu0=(1−h),Shu0=(1−h2/2−h),u(h)=(1−h2/2+O(h4)−h+h3/6+O(h5)). This is a two-component harmonic oscillator with nondimensional q, p and time. Its subflows require only addition and multiplication; the reference is the analytic sine/cosine solution. The first-step formulas already expose the local defect orders. Use the norm of both components to avoid mistaking componentwise cancellation for higher order. This lightweight illustration uses no spatial grid, independent PDE implementation or quantum-chemistry calculation. Global error and observed order at t=1 (two-component Euclidean norm) NhLie–Trotter E(h)pStrang E(h)p 80.1255.220647e-02—2.075134e-03— 160.06252.617930e-020.99585.176511e-042.0032 320.031251.311628e-020.99711.293422e-042.0008 640.0156256.565750e-030.99833.233115e-052.0002 These saved values were recomputed for the fixed input u₀=(1,0), T=1 and N=8,16,32,64. The final global observed orders are 0.9983 for Lie–Trotter and 2.0002 for Strang. A separate single-step check from the exact initial state gives local orders near 2 and 3. Controls check that reversed Lie–Trotter remains first order with a different solution, and that commuting A=−I, B=−2I agrees with exp(−3T) to floating-point roundoff. Conditions: order and stability can be lost The stated orders assume a smooth solution, sufficiently small steps, a fixed finite interval and suitable stability. Shocks, stiff relaxation and nonsmooth initial data can invalidate those expectations. PDE subproblems and their stages need compatible boundary data. Check order reduction from inhomogeneous or time-dependent boundaries separately from spatial and nonlinear-solver errors. A symmetric arrangement alone does not make approximate subflows second order. Standard Strang composition needs subsolvers with at least second-order consistency and sufficiently tight iteration tolerances to retain second order. Exact or symmetric subsolvers are needed to retain time symmetry as well. Direct substitution of forward or backward Euler generally reduces the order to one. Nonautonomous problems require a suitable extended system including time, or consistent subproblem time arguments; freezing everything at the old time is not enough. det⁡Lh=det⁡Sh=1,tr⁡Lh=tr⁡Sh=2−h2,0<∣h∣<2(oscillator). For this oscillator both update matrices have determinant 1 and trace 2−h², giving bounded oscillatory modes for 0<|h|<2. Exact subflows do not by themselves guarantee unconditional stability. Composition inherits only properties preserved by its submaps: Hamiltonian symplecticity does not imply positivity for arbitrary reactions or exact conservation of the full energy. Existing Strang examples and the distinction from IMEX The existing reaction–diffusion finite-amplitude Schnakenberg and saturated-pattern examples use exact half steps of centered-difference diffusion and a full implicit-midpoint reaction step in a Strang composition. Their published records give spatial and temporal checks for those fixed conditions. They are separate from this oscillator illustration, and their distributions, tolerances and results are preserved. IMEX also separates parts of the right-hand side, but IMEX time integration combines explicit and implicit stage equations, whereas the splitting here composes subproblem flows. These are different updates. For the separable-Hamiltonian connection, see symplectic integration. text.ja: 勾配法・準Newton法 勾配法は目的関数の一次情報を、準Newton法は勾配差から作る曲率近似を使います。ここでは滑らかな無制約最小化を扱い、制約付き最適化の最適性条件とは区別します。 対象と代表式 目的関数fの勾配gₖ=∇f(xₖ)、逆Hessian近似Hₖ、探索方向pₖ=−Hₖgₖを使います。BFGSの更新ではs=xₖ₊₁−xₖ、y=gₖ₊₁−gₖ、ρ=1/(yᵀs)です。Hₖ=Iなら最急降下の方向になりますが、単位やスケーリングに依存します。 xk+1=xk−αkHkgk,Hk+1=(I−ρsyT)Hk(I−ρysT)+ρssT. 計算の流れ 勾配を評価し、線探索などでステップ長を選び、曲率情報を更新します。BFGSはHₖ₊₁y=sを満たす対称更新です。Hₖが正定値かつyᵀs>0なら正定値性を維持します。不十分な曲率では更新のスキップや減衰など明示した方策が必要です。 適用条件と落とし穴 非凸問題では局所停留点への収束と大域最適解は別です。ノイズ勾配、非滑らかな目的関数、不正確な内側PDE解法は曲率条件を壊します。相対目的関数変化だけで止めず、勾配ノルム、ステップ、反復上限と終了理由も見ます。 検証するときに見る量 既知解の正定値二次関数で条件数を変え、勾配を方向差分でも照合します。Rosenbrock型の谷では初期値・スケール・線探索を変えます。目的関数が減ったことだけで制約や物理モデルの妥当性は証明できません。 検証済みの実装例：Bratu合成逆問題の随伴勾配による推定 次へ：Bratuの2係数推定・正則化・識別可能性 — この一般解説の既存節を保持し、2係数の実行検証は専用章へ案内します。 公開範囲と関連項目 このページは勾配法・準Newton法の一般的な解説です。実装済みの範囲は、別章のBratu合成逆問題における1次元の箱制約つき射影勾配法とArmijo後退探索です。BFGS・汎用準Newton法や、このページで挙げた一般的な検証案を実装検証した意味ではありません。 勾配法・準Newton法 一次文献・関連資料と確認範囲 原著、後続の変種、著者による著書、概説、公式資料を区別して参照します。DOI・書誌の確認と原文の該当箇所の閲覧を区別し、論文全体の監査や数値再現を行ったという意味ではありません。確認範囲の注記は引用ごとに示します。 R. text.en: Gradient and quasi-Newton optimization Gradient methods use first derivatives; quasi-Newton methods infer curvature from gradient differences. This introduction treats smooth unconstrained minimization, separately from constrained optimality conditions. Problem and representative equations Let gₖ=∇f(xₖ), Hₖ approximate the inverse Hessian and pₖ=−Hₖgₖ. In BFGS, s=xₖ₊₁−xₖ, y=gₖ₊₁−gₖ and ρ=1/(yᵀs). Hₖ=I gives steepest descent in the chosen coordinates, so units and scaling matter. xk+1=xk−αkHkgk,Hk+1=(I−ρsyT)Hk(I−ρysT)+ρssT. Algorithm Evaluate gradients, select a step length using a line search and update curvature. BFGS enforces Hₖ₊₁y=s with a symmetric update. Positive-definite Hₖ and yᵀs>0 preserve positive definiteness. Poor curvature requires an explicit policy such as skipping or damping the update. Conditions and pitfalls For nonconvex problems, finding a local stationary point is different from finding a global optimum. Noisy gradients, nonsmooth objectives and inaccurate inner PDE solves can corrupt curvature. Do not stop on relative objective change alone: inspect gradient norms, step sizes, limits and termination reasons. What to check Vary conditioning on positive-definite quadratics with known minima and check gradients by directional differences. On curved valleys vary initialization, scaling and line searches. Decreasing an objective does not validate physical assumptions or constraints. Verified implementation example: adjoint-gradient fitting of the Bratu synthetic inverse problem Next: two-coefficient Bratu fitting, regularization and identifiability — The existing general-method sections remain; the dedicated chapter contains the two-coefficient execution checks. Publication scope and related entries This page gives general gradient/quasi-Newton reading. Implemented scope is the separate Bratu synthetic inverse example: a scalar box-constrained projected-gradient method with Armijo backtracking. BFGS, general quasi-Newton methods and the broader checks proposed on this page are not implemented or verified by that example. です。平均を引くことで周期適合条件を満たし、ポテンシャルのゼロモードでゲージを固定します。水平平均が実際の鉛直力を生む孤立薄層とは異なります。 PMは質量を格子へ割り当て、Poissonを解き、ポテンシャルを微分して粒子へ加速度を補間します。例は3次元の8近傍節点へのcloud-in-cell（CIC）、連続Fourier Laplacian記号、スペクトル力微分を使います。偶数格子微分では対を持たないNyquistモードをゼロにします。整合したCIC割当て・補間と奇対称力演算子により、選定した周期例で内部力の総和が丸め誤差までゼロになります。 割当て・補間は力を平滑化します。格子Green関数、離散微分、エイリアシング、格子異方性、デコンボリューションが実効相互作用へ影響します。製造した格子モードを正確に解いても、近接対の力精度は示せません。 P³M：近距離を二重計上せず補正する# 粒子・粒子／粒子・格子法は格子力に短距離補正を加えます。 ai=aiPM+∑j∈Ni(aijtarget−aijmesh,near). 引く項は、選んだPM割当て・力演算子、または整合設計の力分割に対応する必要があります。完全なPMへ未修正Newton対力を加えると一部を二重計上します。近傍リストと集積が短距離の計算量を決めます。HockneyのP³Mコード原解説を参照してください。 実用P³M、対応する補正表、適応細分化は未実装です。 Barnes–Hutツリー：近いセルを開く# Barnes・Hut（1986）は粒子を八分木にまとめます。遠方セルは質量分布のモーメントで近似し、近方セルは再帰的に開きます。本実装の幾何受理条件はs/d<thetaで、sはセル辺長、dは重心までの距離です。標的を含むノードは常に開き、直接葉では自己相互作用を除きます。 孤立参照はG=1とPlummer軟化です。 ai=−∑j≠imjxi−xj(∣xi−xj∣2+ϵ2)3/2. ツリーと直接和は粒子、質量、epsilonを同じにします。小thetaは通常、相互作用数を増やして誤差を減らしますが、個別粒子誤差は単調とは限りません。O(N log N)は適切な分布での代表的な尺度で、このPython例の時間測定や最悪計算量の保証ではありません。 多重極：単極と2次モーメント# セル重心から標的へのR、源のずれdelta_a、総質量M、S=sum m_a delta_a delta_a^Tとします。重心の双極は消えます。s²=R²+epsilon²として、同じ軟化核のTaylor展開は、 ϕ(R)≈−G[Ms+3RTSR2s5−tr⁡S2s3]. です。コードはこのポテンシャルを解析微分します。トレースを含む全2次モーメントを残し、非軟化・トレースなし四重極式へ黙って置換すると近似が変わります。図は単極・2次モーメントを同じ直接力和と比較します。 高速多重極法（FMM）は局所展開も作って移動し、セル間相互作用を再利用します。Barnes–Hutへ四重極を加えるだけではありません。Greengard・Rokhlin（1987）が原典で、展開移動は未実装です。 TreePM：別の近距離評価# TreePMは格子長距離場とツリー短距離場を結びます。代表的なGaussianポテンシャル分割は、 ϕ^long=ϕ^ e−k2rs2,ϕshort(r)=−Gmrerfc⁡(r2rs). です。短距離力はこのポテンシャルの微分であり、Newton力にerfcを掛けるだけではありません。打切り、周期性、軟化も分割に整合させます。SpringelのGADGET-2論文が一次例です。ここでの独立したPMとツリーの2例は、TreePM実装を構成しません。 マルチグリッドの位置付け# マルチグリッドは対力の直接和ではなく、離散楕円型方程式を解きます。平滑化で振動誤差を減らし、制限・粗格子解・延長・補正で滑らかな成分を扱います。演算子・境界・粒子結合を指定すれば、粒子格子のPoisson解法を置き換えられます。 既存実装は2次元5点負Laplacian、ゼロDirichlet境界で、孤立3次元粒子重力ではありません。有限孤立格子の境界値には多重極や開放境界構成が使え、近い箱面でphi=0とするだけでは一般に無限遠phi→0を再現しません。 静的な検査を再現する# python scripts/build_particle_gravity.py 図と測定記録を作ります。ツリー例は等質量192粒子、seed17、epsilon=0.03、開口角5種、モーメント次数2種です。誤差は||a_tree−a_direct||₂/||a_direct||₂です。受理ノード数と直接対数を報告しますが、操作コストが異なるため和を時間比較には使いません。 PMは24³周期格子です。別の密度1+0.2cos(2pi x)はG=1でポテンシャル−0.2cos(2pi x)/piを持ちます。テストはCIC質量保存、周期折返し、定数補間、自己力、総力、製造モード、theta=0の厳密開放、選定した力誤差収束を扱います。標的ごとの近似ツリーは対運動量を厳密には保たない場合があるため、記録に総力診断を含めます。 孤立FFTとスラブGreen関数、力と時間積分の追加要件を扱うシンプレクティック写像へ進んでください。 別モデルとして調べる：2次元対数FMM 上の重力・PM・ツリーの本文と境界条件は保持します。以下のFMMは、2次元自由空間の負の対数核を一様四分木で評価する別の教育用モデルです。3次元Coulombや軟化重力の1/r核へ精度を移しません。 旧配布版を保持し、追加版では展開次数と木深さを分けてCartesian直接和・解析配置・保存診断と比較します。深さの単調収束や実測の計算量スケーリング、適応木・周期FMMを検証したとは表示しません。 2次元対数核のM2M・M2L・L2Lを持つFMM 自由空間の対数ポテンシャルを一様四分木の多重極・局所展開で評価し、直接和と比較します。 3次元1/r核、適応木、周期FMM、特異積分、実測の計算量スケーリングは未検証です。2次元自由空間の教育用実装として表示します。 入力・結果・判定 · 解説・式・一次文献 · コード：run.py · コード：electrostatics.py · コード：fmm.py · コード：transport.py · テスト：test_particles.py · 配布ZIP · 保存結果 · text.en: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Particle gravity: PM, P³M, Tree, multipoles, and multigrid Poisson solvers and particle force algorithms answer related questions with different representations. Begin by fixing the Green function, boundary conditions, mass assignment, softening, and force operator. A periodic PM field and an isolated direct-sum field solve different problems, so their raw difference is not a force-accuracy measurement. Particle–mesh: mass to potential to force# In a three-dimensional periodic cube, ∇2ϕ=4πG(ρ−ρ‾),ϕ^(k)=−4πG∣k∣2ρ^(k)(k≠0),ϕ^(0)=0. Subtracting the mean supplies the periodic compatibility condition; setting the potential’s zero mode fixes its gauge. This choice differs from an isolated sheet, whose horizontal mean produces a real vertical force. PM deposits particle masses onto a grid, solves the mesh Poisson equation, differentiates the potential, and interpolates acceleration back to particles. The example uses cloud-in-cell (CIC) weights on eight neighboring mesh nodes in 3D, a continuum Fourier Laplacian symbol, and spectral force derivatives. An even-grid derivative sets its unpaired Nyquist mode to zero. Matched CIC deposition/interpolation and an odd force operator yield zero total internal force to roundoff in the tested periodic example. Assignment and interpolation smooth the force. The mesh Green function, discrete derivative, aliasing, grid anisotropy, and any deconvolution all influence the effective particle interaction. Accurate solution of a manufactured mesh mode does not establish accurate close-pair forces. P³M: correct the near field without counting it twice# Particle–particle/particle–mesh adds a short-range correction to the mesh force: ai=aiPM+∑j∈Ni(aijtarget−aijmesh,near). The subtracted term must correspond to the chosen PM assignment and force operator, or to a consistently designed force split. Adding an unmodified Newtonian pair force to an already complete PM force counts part of the interaction twice. Neighbor lists and clustering determine short-range work. See Hockney’s original P³M code description. A production P³M solver, matching correction table, and adaptive refinements are not implemented here. Barnes–Hut Tree: open the nearby cells# Barnes and Hut (1986) organize particles into an octree. A distant cell is approximated by its mass distribution moments; nearby cells are opened recursively. Our geometric acceptance test is s/d < theta, with cell side s and distance d to its center of mass. A node containing the target is always opened, and direct leaves exclude self-interaction. The implemented isolated reference uses G = 1 and Plummer softening: ai=−∑j≠imjxi−xj(∣xi−xj∣2+ϵ2)3/2. The Tree and direct sum use identical particles, masses, and epsilon. Smaller theta usually trades more interactions for lower error, but individual-particle errors need not decrease monotonically. The familiar O(N log N) description is a typical algorithmic scaling under suitable distributions, not a timing result or worst-case guarantee for this Python example. Multipole expansion: monopole and second moments# Let R point from a cell’s center of mass to the target, delta_a be source offsets, M be total mass, and S = sum m_a delta_a delta_a^T. The center-of-mass dipole vanishes. With s² = R²+epsilon², a Taylor expansion of the same softened kernel gives ϕ(R)≈−G[Ms+3RTSR2s5−tr⁡S2s3]. The code differentiates this potential analytically. It retains the full second moment, including its trace; silently substituting an unsoftened traceless quadrupole formula would change the approximation. The gallery compares monopole and second-moment errors against the same direct force sum. A fast multipole method also forms and translates local expansions, reusing cell-to-cell interactions. It is more than adding a quadrupole to Barnes–Hut. Greengard and Rokhlin (1987) are the original FMM reading reference; FMM translations are not implemented here. TreePM: a different near-field evaluator# TreePM combines a mesh long-range field with a short-range Tree field. A representative Gaussian potential split has ϕ^long=ϕ^ e−k2rs2,ϕshort(r)=−Gmrerfc⁡(r2rs). The short-range force is the derivative of this potential, not merely Newton’s force times erfc. Cutoffs, periodicity, and softening must match the split. Springel’s GADGET-2 paper provides a primary example. The two independent PM and Tree examples here do not constitute an implemented TreePM solver. Where multigrid belongs# Multigrid solves a discretized elliptic equation rather than directly summing particle pairs. A smoother reduces oscillatory error; restriction, a coarse solve, prolongation, and correction address smoother error components. It can replace the grid Poisson solve inside a particle–mesh pipeline, provided its operator, boundary treatment, and particle coupling are specified. The existing multigrid implementation solves a 2D five-point negative-Laplacian problem with zero Dirichlet boundaries. It is not yet the isolated 3D particle-gravity solver. Boundary values for an isolated finite mesh may be supplied by multipoles or another open-boundary construction; setting phi = 0 at a nearby box face generally does not reproduce phi tending to zero at infinity. Reproduce the static checks# python scripts/build_particle_gravity.py This creates the figure and measurement manifest. The Tree experiment uses 192 equal-mass particles, seed 17, epsilon = 0.03, five opening angles, and both moment orders. Its error is ||a_tree−a_direct||₂ / ||a_direct||₂. Counts of accepted nodes and direct pairs are reported; their operation costs differ, so their sum is not a timing comparison. The PM test uses a 24³ periodic mesh. A separate density 1+0.2 cos(2 pi x) has potential −0.2 cos(2 pi x)/pi for G = 1. Tests cover CIC mass conservation, periodic wrapping, constant interpolation, self-force, net force, the manufactured Poisson mode, exact Tree opening at theta = 0, and selected force-error refinements. A target-by-target approximate Tree need not preserve pairwise momentum exactly; the manifest records a net-force diagnostic. Continue with isolated FFT and slab Green functions, and the symplectic map chapter for the additional requirements on force consistency and time integration. A separate model: 2D logarithmic FMM The gravity, PM and tree article and its boundary conventions above are preserved. The following FMM is a separate educational model: a negative-logarithmic kernel in 2D free space evaluated with a uniform quadtree. Its accuracy does not transfer to 3D Coulomb or softened-gravity 1/r kernels. The historical release is retained. The companion separates expansion order from tree depth and compares Cartesian direct sums, analytic configurations and conservation diagnostics. No monotonic error with depth, empirical complexity scaling, adaptive-tree or periodic-FMM validation is claimed. 2D logarithmic FMM with M2M, M2L and L2L Evaluate a free-space log potential with uniform-quadtree multipole and local expansions and compare with direct sums. No 3D 1/r kernel, adaptive tree, periodic FMM, singular quadrature or empirical complexity/scaling study. Evidence applies to this 2D free-space educational implementation. Interaction repartition changes with depth, so fixed-order depth refinement is not assumed monotone. Target-wise expansions need not preserve exact action/reaction. No 3D, adaptive/periodic FMM or complexity-scaling claim. en.title: What a fluid solver would additionally need#

text.ja: 解説章公開コード・データ / Public code and data 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。 粒子法と平滑化粒子流体力学 Lagrange粒子は流れとともに移動しながら量を運びます。SPHは場の値や微分を、局所カーネルで重み付けした粒子和で近似します。独立した初期論文Gingold・Monaghan（1977）とLucy（1977）が歴史的な出発点です。以下の静的再構成は、原著の恒星計算を再現するものではありません。 積分から粒子へ# 平滑化した場を、 fh(x)=∫f(x′)W(x−x′,h) dx′≈∑bmbρbfbW(x−xb,h). で近似します。体積重みm_b/rho_bが重要です。平滑化長hはカーネルの尺度で、必ずしも粒子間隔ではありません。コンパクトな台が近傍探索を定めますが、固定格子の接続を課すわけではありません。 1次元例では、q=|x|/hとして規格化した3次スプラインを使います。 W(x,h)=23h{1−32q2+34q3,0≤q<1,14(2−q)3,1≤q<2,0,q≥2. この係数は1次元のものです。2・3次元では別の規格化定数が必要です。 1の分割と補正# 離散粒子集合では、粒子体積とWの積の総和は1とは限りません。Shepard規格化補間は、その総和で割ります。分母がゼロでなければ定数を再現しますが、この補間補正だけで保存的な運動、線形整合性、安定な圧力力が保証されるわけではありません。 import numpy as np from numart.geometry import sph_reconstruct p = (np.arange(64) + 0.5) / 64 x = np.linspace(0, 1, 201) f, partition = sph_reconstruct(x, p, np.sin(2*np.pi*p), h=0.04) f_corrected, _ = sph_reconstruct(x, p, np.sin(2*np.pi*p), h=0.04, normalize=True) この関数は[0,1]の周期最小像距離と、等しい体積重み1/Nを使います。台が最小像の規約に収まるよう、0<h<1/4が必要です。任意の不等間隔粒子から物理密度を推定するものではありません。 流体ソルバーに追加で必要なもの# 密度推定または連続の式の更新、整合する圧力力、運動量・エネルギー発展、境界粒子、時間積分、近傍探索更新、衝撃波や引張り・ペアリング不安定性の扱いは、追加のモデル選択です。衝撃波捕獲SPHの人工粘性は、物理的なNewton流体の粘性応力テンソルと区別します。 テストでは連続カーネルの規格化と、補正後の離散定数再現を確認します。初版はカーネル再構成のみで、SPH流体ソルバーではありません。時間積分では、粒子kick–drift leapfrogと1階ODEの2ステップleapfrogを混同しない理由を説明します。 粒子重力は別の演算子# PM、P³M、ツリー、多重極は重力場を計算し、SPHカーネルは流体量と微分を再構成します。粒子重力、孤立・スラブ境界核、シンプレクティック時間積分で、自己重力粒子モデルの異なる構成要素を結び付けてください。 Godunov SPH：リーマンソルバーへの分岐# InutsukaのGSPHは粒子流体と粒子対のリーマン問題を結び付けます。2002年の畳み込みによる導出、1994年の先行研究、Iwasaki・Inutsukaの2011年MHD拡張をたどる文献ノートと実装計画です。上のカーネル再構成はGSPH流体計算ではありません。 歴史アトラス →計算結果のギャラリー →
text.en: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Particle methods and smoothed particle hydrodynamics Lagrangian particles carry quantities while moving with a flow. SPH replaces a field value or derivative by a local kernel-weighted particle sum. The independent early papers by Gingold and Monaghan (1977) and Lucy (1977) are historical starting points. The static reconstruction below does not reproduce their stellar calculations. From an integral to particles# A smoothed field is approximated by fh(x)=∫f(x′)W(x−x′,h) dx′≈∑bmbρbfbW(x−xb,h). The volume weight m_b/rho_b matters. Smoothing length h is a kernel scale, not necessarily the particle spacing. Compact support defines the neighbor search; it does not impose a fixed mesh connectivity. Our one-dimensional example uses the normalized cubic spline, with q = |x|/h: W(x,h)=23h{1−32q2+34q3,0≤q<1,14(2−q)3,1≤q<2,0,q≥2. This prefactor is one-dimensional. Two- and three-dimensional kernels require different normalization constants. Partition of unity and correction# The raw sum of particle volumes times W need not equal one on a discrete particle set. A Shepard-normalized interpolant divides by that sum. It reproduces a constant wherever the denominator is nonzero, but this interpolation correction alone does not establish conservative dynamics, linear consistency, or stable pressure forces. import numpy as np from numart.geometry import sph_reconstruct p = (np.arange(64) + 0.5) / 64 x = np.linspace(0, 1, 201) f, partition = sph_reconstruct(x, p, np.sin(2*np.pi*p), h=0.04) f_corrected, _ = sph_reconstruct(x, p, np.sin(2*np.pi*p), h=0.04, normalize=True) The routine uses periodic minimum-image distances on [0,1] and equal volume weights 1/N. It requires 0 < h < 1/4 so the support fits the minimum-image convention. It does not infer physical density from arbitrary unequal particle spacings. What a fluid solver would additionally need# Density estimation or a continuity update, a consistent pressure force, momentum and energy evolution, boundary particles, time stepping, neighbor-search updates, and treatment of shocks or tensile/pairing instabilities are additional modeling decisions. Artificial viscosity used in shock-capturing SPH must be distinguished from the physical Newtonian viscous stress tensor. Tests check the continuous kernel’s normalization and discrete constant reproduction after normalization. This edition implements kernel reconstruction only, not an SPH flow solver. See time integration for why a particle kick–drift leapfrog and a two-step first-order ODE leapfrog should not be conflated. Particle gravity is a separate operator# PM, P³M, Tree, and multipole methods compute gravitational fields; SPH kernels reconstruct fluid quantities and their derivatives. Read particle gravity, isolated and slab boundary kernels, and symplectic time integration to connect these different parts of a self-gravitating particle model. Godunov SPH: the Riemann-solver branch# Inutsuka's GSPH connects particle hydrodynamics with pairwise Riemann problems. The chapter follows the 2002 convolution-based derivation, identifies its 1994 precursor, and links the 2011 MHD extension by Iwasaki and Inutsuka. It is a reading and implementation plan; the kernel reconstruction above is not a GSPH fluid calculation. Historical atlas →Computed gallery →

text.en: On this page Periodic DFT: Γ points, k-point integration, basis sets, SCF and an independent reference A small periodic cell containing one He atom connects Bloch’s theorem, k-point integration, periodic Gaussian bases, auxiliary FFT grids and SCF iteration. A PySCF-backed example is compared with an independent plane-wave DFTK reference, exposing the conventions needed to solve the same model with different discretizations. This educational periodic problem uses nonrelativistic, spin-unpolarized LDA for a fixed simple-cubic He cell. The implementation is a driver using PySCF, rather than a DFT engine written from scratch. It does not optimize crystal structure or predict equilibrium solid helium. Read next: multiatom DFT forces and the BOMD interface Measurements: what was checked, and to what tolerance These stored measurements come from fixed inputs. Case counts describe calculation settings, not distinct physical test problems. Convergence sequences reuse a common baseline. Full results / JSON · Settings and energies / CSV · SCF histories / CSV The fixed physical model and the numerical errors being tested The input is a simple-cubic cell of side 4 bohr containing one He atom at the origin. A local GTH–PADE pseudopotential supplies two valence electrons for a closed-shell, spin-unpolarized Kohn–Sham problem. This He potential has no nonlocal projectors. One example therefore does not validate general multielement crystals or nonlocal pseudopotentials. The geometry is fixed as a teaching configuration for convergence experiments. The exchange-correlation functional is specified explicitly as Libxc LDA_X plus LDA_C_VWN (VWN5). The label LDA alone does not align choices such as VWN and Perdew–Wang correlation. GTH–PADE names the chosen pseudopotential; it does not assert that its generation approximation is identical to the VWN5 used here. Both engines receive the same pseudopotential coefficients and exchange-correlation choice. Atomic units are used, with lattice lengths in bohr and energies in hartree. Total energies are compared per unit cell, including electronic terms and periodic ion–ion interactions. SCF solution error, k-point quadrature, the orbital basis and the auxiliary density/potential grid are varied separately. Reducing these numerical effects does not measure the physical error of LDA or the pseudopotential approximation. [−12∇2+Vloc+VH[n]+Vxc[n]]ψnk=εnkψnk Sources: P. Hohenberg and W. Kohn (1964), W. Kohn and L. J. Sham (1965), S. Goedecker, M. Teter and J. Hutter (1996), S. H. Vosko, L. Wilk and M. Nusair (1980), Libxc developers (2026) Bloch’s theorem and the units of a k point For a periodic potential, an orbital can be written as a plane-wave phase times a lattice-periodic function. The periodic function u and the Bloch orbital ψ are distinct: u is periodic across cell boundaries, whereas ψ satisfies a k-dependent phase boundary condition. Γ is the special point k=0, where this phase is one. Here A contains direct lattice vectors as columns and B contains reciprocal vectors as columns, with AᵀB=2πI. Fractional coordinates κ give the physical wavevector k=Bκ. The coordinates κ are dimensionless; k is in bohr⁻¹ when the lattice is in bohr. PySCF stores cell vectors as rows and passes physical wavevectors to SCF. A shared input lattice and fractional k-point list prevent confusion with DFTK’s column convention. ψnk(r)=eik⋅runk(r),unk(r+R)=unk(r),ψnk(r+R)=eik⋅Rψnk(r) A=(a1,a2,a3),B=2πA−T,k=Bκ,Ω=∣det⁡A∣ Sources: Felix Bloch (1929), PySCF developers (2026), DFTK developers (2026) Γ points and k meshes: quadrature versus band paths Densities and energies of an infinite crystal involve integrals over the Brillouin zone. A finite set of k points and weights approximates these integrals. This example explicitly lists all points of a uniform mesh containing Γ and equal weights summing to one. Γ is included even for even subdivisions. This convention is not automatically identical to software defaults or the half-grid displacement of an even Monkhorst–Pack mesh. Fractional k points differing by an integer reciprocal vector represent the same point. A Γ-only calculation is a one-point quadrature of the Brillouin zone. It can be adequate for some large real-space cells or localized orbitals, but adequacy for this small cell must be measured. Γ-only and several meshes are compared with the same orbital basis, auxiliary grid and SCF settings. Different meshes need not be nested, and monotonically decreasing energy differences are not assumed. A band path joins high-symmetry points to visualize dispersion. Giving its points equal weights generally does not produce a Brillouin-zone quadrature. This example tests integrated energy and density; drawing a band path does not replace k-point convergence. Two-dimensional schematic of Γ-only and uniform k-point sampling. Actual calculations are three-dimensional. 1∣BZ∣∫BZf(k) dk≃∑q=1Nkwqf(kq),∑qwq=1,n(r)=2∑qwq∑n∈occ∣ψnkq(r)∣2 κj=(j1N1,j2N2,j3N3) mod Z3,ji=0,…,Ni−1,wj=1N1N2N3 Sources: H. J. Monkhorst and J. D. Pack (1976), PySCF developers (2026) The orbital basis and auxiliary FFT grid are separate convergence axes The PySCF orbitals expand Bloch sums of Gaussian functions. Results retain basis names such as gth-dzv, the actual function count and overlap conditioning. Increasing a basis’s zeta label does not prove a complete-basis limit; bases with different contractions and polarization functions are not necessarily mathematically nested. Basis differences measure sensitivity within the published finite sequence. FFT density fitting (FFTDF) is an auxiliary plane-wave/FFT representation used for quantities such as density and Coulomb potentials. Refining its mesh does not enlarge the Gaussian orbital space. Conversely, enlarging only the orbital basis cannot remove errors from a coarse auxiliary grid. The PySCF auxiliary grid, DFTK orbital plane-wave cutoff and its associated density grid are distinct, and hartree must not be confused with rydberg. The periodic Coulomb G=0 component is handled with a convention combining electrons, the local pseudopotential and periodic ionic terms. A change in the mean potential also shifts the orbital eigenvalue origin. Even the same physical model needs aligned G=0 constants, pseudopotential corrections, Ewald terms and per-cell versus per-atom units for direct total-energy comparison. Conventions and energy components are checked rather than adding an empirical constant to force agreement. χμk(r)=∑Reik⋅Rχμ(r−R),ψnk=∑μCμn(k)χμk ΔkE,Δorbital basisE,Δauxiliary gridE,Eτ−Etight,EPySCF−EDFTK Sources: S. Goedecker, M. Teter and J. Hutter (1996), PySCF developers (2026), M. F. Herbst, A. Levitt and E. Cancès (2021) SCF residuals, electron count and a sampled KS gap The Kohn–Sham potential depends on density, so an eigenproblem and density update are iterated. Energy changes are supplemented by a commutator residual built from the final density, orbital-equation residuals, orthogonality and electron count. The commutator measure is the maximum over k points of the Frobenius norm of X(FPS−SPF)X, with symmetric orthogonalization X=S⁻¹ᐟ². Orbital residuals use the same final-density F. Results retain iteration histories, stopping reasons and tolerances. Reaching an iteration cap is not labeled convergence. A tolerance sweep changes only SCF settings at fixed discretization and measures the energy difference from a tight solution. This checks the remaining nonlinear solution error. SCF convergence is separate from sufficient orbital bases, auxiliary grids and k points, and from physical-model accuracy. For closed-shell occupations, a sampled KS gap is obtained from the largest occupied and smallest unoccupied eigenvalues over all calculated k points. A positive value indicates separated occupations on that mesh. It neither guarantees the true minimum over the full Brillouin zone nor equals the many-body fundamental gap defined by adding/removing an electron or an experimental optical gap. Unoccupied states also depend on the orbital basis. A visible difference remains between the Gaussian and plane-wave sampled gaps in this example. The independent comparison validates total energies; gap convergence or agreement is not established. FkCk=SkCkεk,Ck†SkCk=I,∑qwqTr⁡(PkqSkq)=Ne=2 Eg,KKS=min⁡k∈K,n∈unoccεnk−max⁡k∈K,n∈occεnk Sources: W. Kohn and L. J. Sham (1965), PySCF developers (2026), DFTK developers (2026) Comparison with an independent DFTK reference in a different basis The example uses PySCF’s periodic integrals, FFTDF and SCF. The independent Julia package DFTK supplies a plane-wave Kohn–Sham reference without calling the teaching PySCF solver. Merely changing an auxiliary representation within PySCF would not be an independent-implementation comparison. Both engines use Libxc for exchange-correlation evaluation, so that component is not independently implemented in this comparison. The lattice, atomic positions, valence count, spin, pseudopotential coefficients, LDA_X plus LDA_C_VWN, fractional k points and weights are aligned. Plane-wave cutoff and SCF convergence are checked on the DFTK side. Gaussian and plane-wave calculations use different finite spaces, so machine-precision agreement is not demanded between their finite-basis energies. Agreement is assessed against the published acceptance width alongside Gaussian-basis and auxiliary-grid sensitivities and reference-cutoff dependence. Meeting this width establishes neither a rigorous bound on true error nor chemical accuracy. Ordinary reproduction against the saved reference and reference regeneration in Julia are separate operations. Input, reference and source hashes and dependency versions are fixed, and execution from an independently extracted ZIP is checked. The release exposes numerical differences, acceptance criteria and convergence sequences as well as the result JSON’s pass flag. Sources: Qiming Sun et al. (2020), M. F. Herbst, A. Levitt and E. Cancès (2021), Libxc developers (2026) First-principles MD: Born–Oppenheimer and Car–Parrinello methods First-principles molecular dynamics (AIMD) moves nuclei using electronic-structure calculations. Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics (BOMD) converges the electronic ground state at each nuclear configuration, then integrates classical nuclear motion using forces on that energy surface. E_BO below includes ionic interactions. The 1927 Born–Oppenheimer paper is cited for electronic–nuclear separation, not as the publication of a modern BOMD program. In BOMD, SCF tolerances must control forces and trajectory reproducibility as well as energies. Atom-centered finite Gaussian bases require force contributions from basis-position dependence (Pulay terms). Finite-difference force checks, timestep refinement and energy drift in unthermostatted NVE trajectories are separate tests. Predicting an electronic initial guess does not remove the requirement to optimize each configuration to adequate accuracy. Car–Parrinello molecular dynamics (CPMD) propagates nuclear coordinates and electronic orbitals together through an extended Lagrangian. The fictitious orbital mass μ is a numerical parameter, rather than the physical electron mass. Lagrange multipliers Λ enforce orthonormality. The displayed convention uses a μ/2 orbital-velocity term at fixed cell and occupations. Generalization to periodic k sampling must consistently include weights and occupations in electronic terms. CPMD orbital propagation does not represent real electronic excitations as in TDDFT. Electronic fictitious motion must remain separated in timescale from nuclear motion, keeping orbitals near the BO surface. Vary μ, timestep and orthogonality tolerance while monitoring fictitious kinetic energy and energy transfer to nuclei. Distinguish the ideal unthermostatted extended-system conserved energy E_ext from nuclear kinetic plus BO energy. These statements do not establish applicability to narrow-gap systems or metals. This section is reading only. This chapter’s fixed one-atom He example validates static total energies and k-point, basis, auxiliary-grid and SCF convergence. Multiatom He forces, energy finite differences, an independent reference and the BOMD force interface are covered in the separate From DFT to atomic forces chapter and release. Long BOMD/CPMD trajectories, timestep/SCF/fictitious-mass sensitivity and thermostats require separate validation. A separate fixed-input educational example executes a short, dimensionless two-state electronic-angle/nuclear-coordinate BO/CP-type model. It does not propagate this chapter’s periodic He calculation or establish general Kohn–Sham BOMD/CPMD, real-material or long-time MD validation. text.ja: この章の目次 DFTから原子間力へ：有限差分・独立参照・力の収束とBOMDへの接続 多原子の周期Heセルで、全エネルギーの位置微分から原子間力を求めます。解析勾配、エネルギーの有限差分、独立した平面波計算を比較し、基底・k点・補助格子・SCFが力に与える影響を分けて確かめます。BOMDへ渡す力の条件と、軌道の検証で追加すべき条件もつなぎます。 固定セル・局所He GTH・スピン非分極LDAの教育用検証です。PySCFの解析核勾配を利用する実行・検証ドライバーであり、自作の電子状態エンジンではありません。この配置の力の一致は、他元素・非局所擬ポテンシャル・応力・長時間BOMDや温度制御の検証を意味しません。 保存した実測値：有限差分・独立参照・力の収束 固定した格子、電子数、汎関数、擬ポテンシャルのもとで、各原子配置における電子基底状態を求めます。Born–Oppenheimerエネルギーは電子項と周期イオン間項を含むセル全体のエネルギーです。原子IのCartesian成分αに働く力は、その座標についての全微分に負号を付けた値です。勾配と力の符号を区別し、座標をbohr、エネルギーをhartreeで扱うと力の単位はhartree/bohrになります。 Pulay (1969), PySCF developers (2026) 力について基底・k点・補助格子・SCFを別々に収束させる エネルギー差が小さくなったという理由だけで、力も十分に収束したと判断しません。Gaussian軌道基底、Brillouinゾーンのk点メッシュ、FFTの補助格子、SCF停止条件を1つずつ変え、同じ原子・成分の力の差を測ります。基準と比べるときは原子の順序とCartesian軸を固定します。今回の要約は全成分の絶対値最大を用いるL∞型のノルムで、原子ごとのベクトル長や成分平均とは区別します。 基底名のzeta数を増やす系列は、必ずしも入れ子の空間や単調な力の変化を与えません。k点メッシュもすべてが入れ子ではありません。最後の2設定の力の差を公開した目安と比較しますが、それを完全基底や無限k点での厳密な誤差上界とは呼びません。密度や局所ポテンシャルを載せる補助FFT格子は、Gaussianの軌道空間と独立の収束軸です。 SCFの未収束は力にも現れます。終了フラグと反復回数だけでなく、電子数、軌道・SCF残差など、保存した状態の診断量を併せて読みます。厳しい停止条件に対して力が変わらないことを直接測り、未収束の電子状態をBOMDへ正常な力として返さないようにします。 各走査は1つの制御値だけを変え、その他の制御値は公開入力で指定した有限の設定に固定します。Γ点と2³では基底系列もそれぞれ確認しますが、4³・最大Gaussian基底・最細FFTを同時に組み合わせた完全な収束計算は行っていません。独立参照との一致もΓ点と2³の指定ケースに限られます。 ∥ΔF∥∞=max⁡I,α∈{x,y,z}∣FIα(a)−FIα(b)∣ ΔbasisF,ΔkF,ΔFFTF,Fτ−Ftight 関連出典：PySCF developers (2026), DFTK developers (2026), J. text.en: On this page From DFT to atomic forces: finite differences, independent references, force convergence and the BOMD interface Atomic forces are obtained as position derivatives of the total energy in a multiatom periodic He cell. Analytic gradients, finite differences of energies and an independent plane-wave calculation are compared, separating orbital-basis, k-point, auxiliary-grid and SCF effects on forces. The requirements for a BOMD force interface are distinguished from the additional validation of trajectories. This educational verification uses a fixed cell, a local He GTH potential and spin-unpolarized LDA. It is an execution and validation driver using PySCF analytic nuclear gradients, rather than a new electronic-structure engine. Agreement for this configuration does not validate other elements, nonlocal pseudopotentials, stress, long BOMD trajectories or thermostats. Stored measurements: finite differences, independent references and force convergence These stored results come from the release’s fixed input. Force comparisons use the maximum absolute difference over Cartesian components in hartree/bohr unless stated otherwise. Sweeps reuse common settings; setting counts are not distinct physical problems. Acceptance uses unrounded values. Wide numeric tables scroll horizontally within their own region. Feynman (1939) The Hellmann–Feynman theorem and Pulay terms from moving bases For a normalized exact eigenstate, the energy derivative with respect to a parameter equals the expectation of the Hamiltonian derivative. This is the Hellmann–Feynman relation. Feynman’s 1939 paper is a historical primary source for evaluating molecular forces directly. The theorem alone does not make every force correct for an electronic state represented in a finite atom-centered basis. The H and Ψ below express the general theorem; they do not replace the Kohn–Sham total energy by a sum of orbital eigenvalues. A Gaussian basis moving with the atoms changes its functions and overlap matrix when nuclei move. Even with variationally optimized orbital coefficients, derivatives of this basis dependence must be included when differentiating the discrete energy. These are Pulay terms. The overlap derivative contracted with an energy-weighted density in the generalized eigenproblem is one contribution. The driver uses PySCF analytic nuclear gradients; it does not substitute a bare electron–ion Coulomb force. At fixed cell and cutoff, plane waves do not move with atomic positions. Finite-cutoff force errors nevertheless remain, and SCF and density-grid errors must still be controlled. The absence of moving-atom basis terms does not make plane-wave forces exact. At each displaced geometry the SCF is converged independently, and the resulting total energies give a central-difference force. The lattice, k points and weights, basis name, FFT grid, functional, pseudopotential and electron count are aligned. The atom-centered basis moves too, so this probes derivatives of the same discrete energy including basis-position dependence. For a smooth energy surface, central-difference truncation is O(h²). SCF solution and roundoff errors in energies are divided by 2h, so very small displacements can increase errors. Several h values are retained to locate a stable agreement range with analytic forces. A clean U-shaped measured curve is not assumed. An input SCF energy tolerance is not interpreted as a rigorous bound on the error of each energy. text.ja: Particle-in-Cell（PIC） プラズマPICは速度分布を代表粒子で、自己無撞着な場を格子で表現します。粒子同士のCoulomb力をすべて直接足す方法とは、平滑化・衝突性・統計誤差が異なります。 対象と代表式 まず非相対論的・静電的なVlasov–Poisson系を考えます。代表粒子pの重みwₚ、電荷qₚ、位置xₚから格子電荷ρᵢを作ります。Sᵢは粒子形状から得る無次元割当係数でΣᵢSᵢ=1、Vᵢはセル体積です。E=−∇φとし、Poisson方程式を同じ境界条件で解きます。 ρi=1Vi∑pwpqpSi(xp),−∇h2ϕi=ρi/ϵ0,v˙p=(qp/mp)Eh(xp). 計算の流れ 電荷の割当、Poisson解法、電場の粒子位置への補間、粒子の押し出しを繰り返します。背景イオンもρに含めます。電磁PICへ進む場合は電流割当とMaxwell更新を加え、離散連続の式との整合を確認します。Dawsonのシート模型は歴史的な粒子プラズマの例であり、全PIC方式の定義ではありません。 適用条件と落とし穴 陽的静電PICではプラズマ振動の時間尺度とDebye長の解像を調べます。必要条件は押し出し法・形状・場の解法で変わり、万能なΔtやセル幅はありません。粒子数を増やす統計収束と格子/時間刻みの収束を分け、自己力・有限格子加熱にも注意します。 追加版は静止した一様イオン背景を持つ1次元周期・静電cold-electron PICです。CIC割当・補間、Poisson場と粒子押し出しの固定例であり、熱的Landau減衰、電磁PIC、イオン運動は対象外です。 検証するときに見る量 単一粒子の自己力、中性一様分布、微小振幅のプラズマ振動やLandau減衰から始めます。総電荷、エネルギードリフト、粒子数依存と独立乱数系列を報告します。減衰率は理論の線形振幅域に限って比較します。 線形の冷たいプラズマ振動を小振幅の参照とし、格子・時間刻み・粒子数を分けて比較します。総電荷、場の残差、自己力、粒子運動量と粒子・場エネルギーの診断を別々に示します。保存診断の小ささだけで軌道精度や任意の長時間安定性を保証しません。 追加版では固定CIC空間系の運動をDOP853でも積分し、公差と最大刻みの感度を調べます。これは時間積分の別アルゴリズムによる照合であり、独立した連続Vlasov–Poissonソルバーではありません。粒子数の乱数検査は初期時刻の単一Fourier電荷モードのpowerが対象で、CICの有限格子応答を含めて解析期待値と比較します。粒子数増大による任意の非線形軌道の収束とは区別します。 固定入力で確かめる：別々の配布版 各例の入力・観測量・診断の定義と適用範囲を確認します。検査の合格が示す内容は受入条件によって異なり、数学的な一般保証とは区別します。旧版の入力・測定・公差は保持します。 CIC静電PICの冷たいプラズマ振動 固定した標的の計算例 1次元周期セルの電子をCICで格子と結び、Poisson方程式と粒子運動を自洽に進めます。 有限振幅・有限粒子数の誤差床があります。非線形不安定性、Landau減衰、衝突、電磁PIC、相対論粒子、境界流入出の検証ではありません。 入力・結果・受入条件 · 手法・式・一次文献 · コード：run.py · コード：electrostatics.py · コード：fmm.py · コード：transport.py · テスト：test_particles.py · 配布ZIP · 保存結果 text.en: Particle-in-cell / PIC Plasma PIC represents a distribution by computational particles and self-consistent fields by a mesh. Its smoothing, collisionality and sampling error differ from direct all-pairs Coulomb dynamics. Problem and representative equations Start with nonrelativistic electrostatic Vlasov–Poisson. Computational particle p has weight wₚ, charge qₚ and position xₚ. Dimensionless shape weights Sᵢ sum to one, and Vᵢ is cell volume. Deposit ρ, solve Poisson with the stated boundary conditions, and use E=−∇φ. ρi=1Vi∑pwpqpSi(xp),−∇h2ϕi=ρi/ϵ0,v˙p=(qp/mp)Eh(xp). Algorithm Repeat charge deposition, field solution, particle gathering and particle pushing; include background ions in ρ. Electromagnetic PIC additionally needs current deposition and Maxwell updates consistent with discrete continuity. Dawson’s sheet model is a historical particle-plasma example, not the definition of every PIC discretization. Conditions and pitfalls Explicit electrostatic PIC must examine plasma-frequency time scales and Debye-length resolution. Exact restrictions depend on the particle pusher, shape and field solver. Separate sampling convergence in particle count from grid/time convergence, and check self-force and finite-grid heating. The companion is one-dimensional periodic electrostatic cold-electron PIC with a fixed uniform ion background. It is a fixed CIC deposit/gather, Poisson-field and particle-push example; thermal Landau damping, electromagnetic PIC and moving ions are outside its scope. What to check Begin with single-particle self-force, a uniform neutral distribution, and small-amplitude plasma oscillations or Landau damping. Report charge, energy drift, particle-count dependence and independent random realizations. Compare damping rates only within the linear-amplitude regime used by the theory. Use linear cold-plasma oscillation as a small-amplitude reference and vary mesh, time step and particle count separately. Report charge, field residual, self-force, particle momentum and particle-plus-field energy diagnostics separately. Small conservation diagnostics alone guarantee neither trajectory accuracy nor arbitrary long-time stability. The companion also integrates the fixed CIC spatial system with DOP853 and tests tolerance/maximum-step sensitivity. This is an alternative time-integration algorithm, not an independent continuum Vlasov–Poisson solver. The random particle-count check concerns the initial power of one Fourier charge mode, compared with its analytic expectation including the finite-grid CIC response. It is distinct from particle-count convergence of arbitrary nonlinear trajectories. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Cold-plasma oscillation with electrostatic CIC PIC Computation for a fixed target Couple electrons to a 1D periodic grid by CIC, solving Poisson and particle motion self-consistently. Finite amplitude and finite particles leave an error floor. Nonlinear instabilities, Landau damping, collisions, electromagnetic/relativistic PIC and open particle boundaries are unvalidated. text.ja: PINN・ニューラル演算子 PINNは特定の問題の近似解をニューラル関数として学習し、neural operatorは係数場や初期条件から解の関数への写像を学びます。同じニューラルネットでも、学習対象と検証方法が違います。 対象と代表式 PINNではu_θのPDE残差、境界残差、データ残差を重みλで足した経験損失を最小化します。NとBはPDE・境界演算子、f,gは与えた右辺です。FNOはvを特徴関数とし、Fourier空間の積分核Kと局所作用Wを組み合わせる層の代表形を使います。 L(θ)=λr⟨∣N[uθ]−f∣2⟩r+λb⟨∣B[uθ]−g∣2⟩b+λd⟨∣uθ−uobs∣2⟩d. vℓ+1=σ ⁣(Wℓvℓ+F−1[Kℓ Fvℓ]). 計算の流れ PINNでは領域と単位をスケーリングし、自動微分で残差を作り、学習点と境界条件の課し方を指定して最適化します。FNOでは入力・参照解の集合で写像を学習し、Fourierモードを有限数に切ります。原PINN論文とFNO論文は別の提案です。 適用条件と落とし穴 小さい訓練損失は、領域全体の小さい解誤差や保存則の保証ではありません。残差項の不均衡、衝撃波、硬い尺度、学習分布外の入力を調べます。格子間転送の可能性と、任意解像度で正しい物理を再現する保証も区別します。 検証するときに見る量 解析解または独立に収束させた従来法と比較し、学習点外のL1/L2/L∞誤差、境界・保存則、複数seedを測ります。operator学習では同じ軌道の近接時刻を無作為分割するだけでなく、問題単位でtrain/testを分け、入力分布外も別報告します。 選択閲読した原典と今回の小例 2017年PINN Part I preprintの§2では、残差とデータ・境界の損失を区別します。FNO v3（2021年）§3–4の層は局所線形作用とFourier積分作用に非線形活性化を組み合わせます。今回の小Poisson・周期拡散は別の教育用入力で、2019年JCP論文全文や原著の大規模実験・性能を再現したものではありません。 公開範囲と関連項目 既存の教育用コードと版を固定した検証記録への案内です。今回の本文・翻訳の追加でコードや過去の測定結果を変更せず、原論文全体の再現を主張しません。 PINN・ニューラル演算子 一次文献・関連資料と確認範囲 原著、後続の変種、著者による著書、概説、公式資料を区別して参照します。DOI・書誌の確認と原文の該当箇所の閲覧を区別し、論文全体の監査や数値再現を行ったという意味ではありません。確認範囲の注記は引用ごとに示します。 M. text.en: PINNs and neural operators A PINN fits a neural representation of a particular solution; a neural operator learns a map from input functions such as coefficients or initial data to solution functions. Their targets and validation protocols differ. Problem and representative equations A PINN minimizes an empirical weighted loss of PDE, boundary and data residuals. N and B are differential/boundary operators and f,g are prescribed data. A representative FNO layer combines a Fourier-parameterized integral operator K with a local map W acting on feature functions v. L(θ)=λr⟨∣N[uθ]−f∣2⟩r+λb⟨∣B[uθ]−g∣2⟩b+λd⟨∣uθ−uobs∣2⟩d. vℓ+1=σ ⁣(Wℓvℓ+F−1[Kℓ Fvℓ]). Algorithm For a PINN, scale coordinates/units, differentiate residuals, specify collocation points and boundary enforcement, and optimize. FNO trains an operator on input/reference-solution pairs and truncates Fourier modes. Cite the PINN and FNO papers as separate proposals. Conditions and pitfalls Small training loss is not a bound on global solution error or conservation. Examine residual imbalance, shocks, stiff scales and out-of-distribution inputs. Transfer between discretizations is not a guarantee of physical correctness at arbitrary resolution. What to check Compare against analytic or independently converged conventional solutions. Measure off-training L1/L2/L∞ errors, boundaries, conservation and multiple seeds. Split operator data by independent problems rather than nearby time slices alone, and report distribution-shift tests separately. Selected original sources and the present small examples Selected section 2 of the 2017 PINN Part I preprint distinguishes residual loss from data and boundary losses. Sections 3–4 of FNO version 3 (2021) combine a local linear map, a Fourier integral map and nonlinear activation. The present small Poisson and periodic-heat inputs are separate educational choices. Neither the full 2019 JCP article nor the original large experiments or performance claims are reproduced. text.ja: Particle Mesh Ewald（PME） PMEはEwald法の逆空間項を粒子から格子へ移し、FFTを使う方法です。原PMEのLagrange補間と、後のSPMEのB-spline補間を区別して読みます。 対象と代表式 中性・3次元周期のCoulomb系で、格子点xₘに割り当てた電荷Qₘを考えます。Wₘは割当重み、ĜₕはEwaldのGaussian因子、格子規約、補間補正を含む逆空間作用素です。この模式式は逆空間部分だけで、実空間・自己項を置き換えません。 Qm=∑iqiWm(ri),ϕh=Fh−1 ⁣[G^h FhQ]. 計算の流れ 原法では局所Lagrange補間で電荷を格子へ割り当て、離散Fourier変換、格子上の畳み込み、逆変換を行います。力の微分方法と粒子への補間を一組として定義します。格子上で得た電場とエネルギー微分の力が、選んだ離散化で一致するとは限りません。 適用条件と落とし穴 格子を細かくする誤差、補間次数、Ewaldの打切り、力の微分規約を混ぜずに比較します。FFTの正規化とk=0、単位を明記します。O(N log N)は通常の格子増大の仮定を伴う計算量の説明で、精度の保証ではありません。 ここで結ぶ公開コードの採用形はB-splineの解析的エネルギー勾配を使うsmooth PMEです。1993年のLagrange補間PMEを実装・検証したという意味ではなく、元のPMEの式・文献・適用条件を保って別の採用変種へ案内します。 検証するときに見る量 同一の小さい中性セルについて、十分収束した直接Ewald和を参照にします。格子数・補間次数・分割定数を変え、エネルギーと力のRMS/最大誤差、平行移動依存性を調べます。重力PMの成功をPMEの検証に流用しません。 追加版では同じ中性周期電荷に対し格子数・B-spline order・共通平行移動を変え、収束した直接Ewaldと別実装theta積分に比較します。直接Ewaldとの共有実空間・自己項があるため、その一致だけを独立な全エネルギー検証とはしません。 固定入力で確かめる：別々の配布版 各例の入力・観測量・診断の定義と適用範囲を確認します。検査の合格が示す内容は受入条件によって異なり、数学的な一般保証とは区別します。旧版の入力・測定・公差は保持します。 text.en: Particle mesh Ewald / PME PME transfers the reciprocal Ewald calculation to a mesh and uses FFTs. Distinguish the original Lagrange-interpolation PME from the later B-spline construction of SPME. Problem and representative equations For a neutral triply periodic Coulomb system, Qₘ is charge assigned to mesh point xₘ using weights Wₘ. The reciprocal operator Ĝₕ includes Ewald screening, mesh conventions and interpolation corrections. This schematic describes only the reciprocal contribution; real-space and self terms remain necessary. Qm=∑iqiWm(ri),ϕh=Fh−1 ⁣[G^h FhQ]. Algorithm Assign charges with local Lagrange polynomials, transform the mesh, apply the reciprocal convolution and transform back. Specify the differentiation and particle-gather rules together. A mesh-interpolated field and the derivative of the discrete energy need not give identical forces. Conditions and pitfalls Separate mesh resolution, interpolation order, Ewald cutoffs and force differentiation in error studies. State FFT normalization, k=0 treatment and units. The usual O(N log N) description assumes an appropriate mesh-growth regime and is not an accuracy guarantee. The linked implementation adopts smooth PME with B-spline analytical energy gradients. It does not implement or validate the original 1993 Lagrange-interpolation PME; the original PME equations, sources and applicability remain distinct from this implemented variant. What to check Use a converged direct Ewald calculation for the identical neutral cell. Vary mesh size, interpolation order and screening; measure RMS/maximum energy and force errors and sensitivity to common translations. A gravity-PM test does not validate PME. The companion varies mesh size, B-spline order and common translation for the same neutral periodic charges, comparing against converged direct Ewald and a separately implemented theta integral. The direct-Ewald comparison shares real-space/self terms, so agreement there alone is not independent validation of the entire energy. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Mesh/order convergence of B-spline smooth PME Computation for a fixed target A small smooth-PME example assigns charge with B-splines and evaluates the Ewald reciprocal contribution by FFT. Finite-mesh aliasing permits nonzero net force for this energy-gradient variant; that diagnostic is reported. No exact momentum conservation, long MD, original PME, optimized P³M or slab validation is claimed. text.ja: QR・SVD・最小二乗 最小二乗、低ランク近似、条件数の診断には、同じ行列でも異なる分解が役立ちます。QRは直交化と三角系へ、SVDは特異値と可解な方向へ問題を分けます。 対象と代表式 m≥nの実行列Aに対する薄いQRではQᵀQ=I、Rは上三角です。列フルランクなら最小二乗解はRx=Qᵀbで求まります。SVDのσᵢは非負の特異値で、閾値以下を切る疑似逆行列は、元と同じ問題ではなく正則化した問題を解きます。 A=QR=UΣVT,min⁡x∥Ax−b∥2,A+b=∑σi>τuiTbσivi(truncated). 計算の流れ Householder反射で列の下側を消すQRは、通常のGram–Schmidtより直交性を保ちやすい構成です。ランク診断には列ピボットやSVDを検討します。SVDは直交変換で二重対角へ落としてから処理する代表方式があり、正規方程式を明示的に作る必要はありません。 適用条件と落とし穴 2ノルムではκ₂(AᵀA)=κ₂(A)²となり、正規方程式は条件を悪化させます。小さい残差でも、悪条件やノイズがあれば係数は不確かです。ランクの閾値はスケール・丸め・観測誤差に応じて定め、単位の違う列のスケーリングも検討します。 残差・後退誤差と、求めた係数・特異値の前進誤差を区別します。条件数が大きければ、入力や右辺の小さな摂動が係数を大きく変えることがあります。数値階数は特異値の閾値と精度に依存する規約で、階数を切り捨てた最小二乗解は元と同じ問題の厳密解とは限りません。 一般の最小二乗問題では、条件数だけでなく右辺と列空間の角度にも感度が依存します。片側Jacobi SVDの高い相対精度に関する文献上の結果にも、停止規準や成分ごとの条件付けという仮定があります。今回の小行列で微小特異値が一致しても、任意の悪条件行列への万能な相対精度を意味しません。 検証するときに見る量 A−QR、QᵀQ−I、A−UΣVᵀの相対ノルム、最小二乗の正規性Aᵀ(Ax−b)を調べます。特異値が既知の行列とランク欠損例で、入力摂動に対する解の変化も比較します。 追加版では既知の特異値を持つ小行列、右辺の固定摂動、階数判定の閾値を用い、条件数に沿って誤差を比較します。QR・SVDの再構成と直交性、最小二乗残差、係数の前進誤差、数値階数を別々に測ります。LAPACK参照に加え、実際の二進浮動小数点入力を高精度演算に移した独立参照を区別します。正規方程式による条件数の二乗化は上の理論説明であり、この追加例で実行した対照とはしません。 固定入力で確かめる：別々の配布版 各例の入力・観測量・診断の定義と適用範囲を確認します。検査の合格が示す内容は受入条件によって異なり、数学的な一般保証とは区別します。旧版の入力・測定・公差は保持します。 Householder QRと片側Jacobi SVD：直交性・階数・最小二乗 固定した標的の計算例 実の縦長行列に対するHouseholder QRと片側Jacobi SVDを自作し、通常行列・列スケール差10⁶の行列・階数落ち行列を検査します。独立LAPACKの特異値と最小ノルム最小二乗解を照合します。 完全なLAPACK置換、複素行列、横長行列、任意の極端なスケール、最適な相対特異値精度を保証しません。10⁻¹²未満の特異値は入力した数値階数の規約で打ち切るため、数学的な厳密階数と区別します。Demmel–Veselićの精度定理の全条件を実証したとは主張しません。 入力・結果・受入条件 · 手法・式・一次文献 · コード：run.py · コード：solvers.py · text.en: QR, SVD and least squares Least squares, low-rank approximation and conditioning call for different matrix decompositions. QR reduces a problem to orthogonal transformations and a triangular solve; SVD exposes singular values and resolvable directions. Problem and representative equations For a real m×n matrix with m≥n, thin QR has QᵀQ=I and upper triangular R. Full column rank gives the least-squares solve Rx=Qᵀb. SVD has nonnegative singular values σᵢ. Truncating small σᵢ in a pseudoinverse regularizes the problem and can change the solution being sought. A=QR=UΣVT,min⁡x∥Ax−b∥2,A+b=∑σi>τuiTbσivi(truncated). Algorithm Householder QR eliminates subdiagonal entries with reflections and generally maintains orthogonality better than classical Gram–Schmidt. Consider column pivoting or SVD for rank diagnosis. Classical SVD algorithms reduce to bidiagonal form using orthogonal transformations rather than explicitly forming normal equations. Conditions and pitfalls For full column rank, κ₂(AᵀA)=κ₂(A)². A small residual can coexist with uncertain coefficients under ill-conditioning or noise. Choose a numerical-rank threshold relative to scale, rounding and measurement uncertainty, and consider column scaling when variables have different units. Distinguish residual/backward error from forward errors in coefficients or singular values. At large condition numbers, small changes to the input or right-hand side can cause large coefficient changes. Numerical rank depends on a singular-value threshold and arithmetic precision; a truncated least-squares solution need not solve the original problem exactly. General least-squares sensitivity also depends on the angle between the right-hand side and the column space, not only on condition number. Published relative-accuracy results for one-sided Jacobi SVD depend on stopping rules and componentwise conditioning. Agreement for small singular values in these small matrices is not a universal relative-accuracy guarantee for arbitrary ill-conditioned matrices. What to check Check relative factorization residuals, orthogonality and Aᵀ(Ax−b). Test prescribed singular values and rank-deficient cases, and compare solution changes under controlled data perturbations. The added release compares errors across small matrices with prescribed singular values, fixed right-hand-side perturbations and numerical-rank thresholds. Measure QR/SVD reconstruction and orthogonality, least-squares residual, coefficient forward error and numerical rank separately. Distinguish LAPACK references from independent high-precision references constructed from the actual binary floating-point input. Condition-number squaring for normal equations is explained above as theory; it is not an executed control in this added case. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Householder QR and one-sided Jacobi SVD: orthogonality, rank and least squares Computation for a fixed target Original Householder QR and one-sided Jacobi SVD for real tall matrices are checked on ordinary, 10⁶-column-scaled and rank-deficient inputs, against separate LAPACK singular values and minimum-norm least-squares solutions. Not a full LAPACK replacement or validation of complex/wide matrices, arbitrary extreme scales or optimal relative singular-value accuracy. The 10⁻¹² cutoff defines numerical rather than exact mathematical rank. The experiment does not establish all hypotheses of the Demmel–Veselić accuracy results. Input, results and acceptance · Method, equations and sources · Code: run.py · Code: solvers.py · Tests: test_foundations.py · Release ZIP · Saved results · Independent-extraction rerun receipt QR/SVD: prescribed spectra, perturbation gain and numerical rank Computation for a fixed target Vary condition number from 1 to 2³⁶ for exactly representable 16×4 dyadic matrices, separating reconstruction from forward solution error. Compare LAPACK and separately executed 80/120-digit references for the actual binary64 inputs. Some LAPACK and projected-core numerical infrastructure is shared. mpmath SVD uses separate bidiagonalization and QR iteration; mpmath least squares is a separate high-precision implementation of the same Householder family. Tiny-singular-value relative accuracy is not guaranteed for arbitrary ill-conditioned matrices. text.ja: Gauss求積・適応積分 Gauss求積は重みに適合する節点と重みを選び、少ない点数で多項式積分を正確にします。適応積分は区間ごとの誤差推定を使って評価点を配分する別の考え方です。 対象と代表式 正の重みw(x)に対するn点Gauss則は、条件が整えば次数2n−1以下の多項式に厳密です。直交多項式の三項漸化係数で作るJacobi行列Jの固有値が節点、正規化固有ベクトルvの第1成分の二乗とμ₀=∫wが求積重みになります。 ∫abf(x)w(x) dx≈∑j=1nωjf(xj),Jvj=xjvj,ωj=μ0(vj)12. 計算の流れ Golub–Welsch法はこの対称三重対角固有値問題を解きます。適応Gauss–Kronrod型では入れ子の2つの則の差を局所誤差の指標にし、区間を分割して絶対/相対許容誤差と照合します。両者の差は厳密な誤差上界とは限りません。 適用条件と落とし穴 点特異性、不連続、高速振動、広い領域の細いピークでは、評価点が構造を見落とします。既知の不連続で区間を分け、必要なら変数変換や重み付き則を使います。積分値が0に近いと相対誤差だけの停止判定は不適切です。 積分が相殺で小さくなるときは、∫|f|/|∫f|のような相殺条件数も有用です。絶対誤差・相対誤差と、積分則内部の誤差推定値は別の量です。有限個の評価点が狭い山をすべて見逃す対照では、二つの近似の差が小さくても真の積分誤差が大きくなり得ます。 条件数を比べるときは入力摂動のノルムと摂動モデルを明示し、積分値が0なら相対条件数・相対誤差を未定義として絶対量で評価します。 検証するときに見る量 単項式の厳密積分で厳密次数を確認し、解析積分できる非多項式、特異点と細いピークでも試します。推定誤差と真の誤差、評価回数、分割上限到達の終了理由を分けて残します。 追加版では求積点数・許容誤差を変え、既知の積分値を持つ滑らかな関数、相殺を伴う関数、固定した狭い山の対照を独立参照と比較します。真の誤差、推定誤差、関数評価回数を分けて記録します。狭い山を明示的に分割して捉える計算と見逃す診断対照を区別し、全ての被積分関数への誤差保証とはしません。 端点で導関数が特異になる例は変数変換の前後を比較し、評価回数や再帰深さの上限への到達も終了状態として残します。 固定入力で確かめる：別々の配布版 各例の入力・観測量・診断の定義と適用範囲を確認します。検査の合格が示す内容は受入条件によって異なり、数学的な一般保証とは区別します。旧版の入力・測定・公差は保持します。 Gauss–Legendreと適応求積：厳密次数・推定誤差・予算切れ 固定した標的の計算例 Legendreの3項漸化式からGauss節点と重みを構成し、2n−1次までの多項式モーメントと指数関数を検査します。適応Simpsonは指数関数とLorentz型ピークを積分し、解析積分・独立QUADPACKと比較します。 Simpsonの局所推定は任意の関数に対する厳密な誤差上界ではありません。高周波の見落とし、特異点、丸め誤差の停滞を一般に解決する実装ではなく、Gauss–KronrodやQUADPACK全体の再実装でもありません。 入力・結果・受入条件 · 手法・式・一次文献 · コード：run.py · コード：solvers.py · テスト：test_foundations.py · 配布ZIP · text.en: Gaussian and adaptive quadrature Gaussian quadrature selects nodes and weights for a measure to integrate polynomials efficiently. Adaptive integration separately allocates function evaluations using local error estimates. Problem and representative equations For a positive measure, an n-point Gaussian rule is exact through degree 2n−1 when the required moments exist. The Jacobi matrix J of orthogonal-polynomial recurrence coefficients has quadrature nodes as eigenvalues. Weights are μ₀ times squared first components of normalized eigenvectors, with μ₀=∫w. ∫abf(x)w(x) dx≈∑j=1nωjf(xj),Jvj=xjvj,ωj=μ0(vj)12. Algorithm Golub–Welsch solves this symmetric tridiagonal eigenproblem. Adaptive Gauss–Kronrod-type integration uses differences between nested rules to estimate local errors, subdivides intervals and checks absolute/relative tolerances. The rule difference is not an unconditional error bound. Conditions and pitfalls Singularities, jumps, rapid oscillations and narrow peaks can be missed by sampled nodes. Split at known discontinuities and consider transformations or matched weighted rules. Relative tolerance alone is unsuitable when the integral is close to zero. When cancellation makes an integral small, a cancellation condition number such as integral(|f|)/|integral(f)| is informative. Absolute/relative true errors differ from a rule’s internal error estimate. If finitely many sample points miss a narrow bump, agreement between two approximations can coexist with a large true integration error. State the input-perturbation norm and perturbation model when comparing condition numbers; if the integral is zero, relative condition and relative error are undefined, so report absolute quantities. What to check Verify degree of exactness on monomials, then test nonpolynomials with known integrals, singularities and narrow peaks. Record estimated versus true error, evaluation count and termination caused by subdivision limits. The added release varies rule order and tolerance for smooth functions with known integrals, cancellation-sensitive functions and a fixed narrow-bump control. Compare against independent references and record true error, estimated error and function evaluations separately. Distinguish an explicitly split calculation that resolves the bump from a missed-bump diagnostic; neither supplies a universal guarantee for all integrands. Compare an endpoint-derivative singularity before and after a change of variables, and retain evaluation/depth-budget exhaustion as an explicit termination status. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Gauss–Legendre and adaptive quadrature: exactness, error estimates and budgets Computation for a fixed target Construct Gaussian nodes/weights from the Legendre recurrence and test polynomial moments through degree 2n−1 and an exponential. Adaptive Simpson integrates exponential and Lorentzian peaks, against analytic integrals and independent QUADPACK. The local Simpson estimate is not a rigorous error bound for arbitrary functions. The implementation does not generally solve missed high frequencies, singularities or roundoff stagnation, and it is not a reimplementation of Gauss–Kronrod or all of QUADPACK. The Simpson estimate is not a certified error bound. Passing the blind-spot control does not mean accurate integration. Direct square-root integration may honestly terminate at its depth budget. Exhaustive oscillatory/singular exploration and certified quadrature are not claimed. (1980) 時間依存DFT TDDFTは時間依存密度の理論です。下式は局所ポテンシャルを使う時間依存KSの代表形で、初期状態依存や交換相関の記憶効果は一般には残ります。実時間伝播と、基底状態の周りの線形応答計算を区別します。 線形応答では励起エネルギーや振動子強度、実時間では外場・時間刻み・伝播時間・吸収スペクトルへの変換条件を保存します。断熱近似は汎関数の時間依存の近似です。 i∂tϕi(r,t)=[−12∇2+vs[n](r,t)]ϕi(r,t) 基底状態のKS固有値差だけをTDDFTの励起エネルギーと呼びません。二重励起・長距離電荷移動等は選んだ近似の限界を確認します。 条件・実装状況・JSON Runge, E.; Gross, E. text.en: ELECTRONIC STRUCTURE · QUANTUM CHEMISTRY · DFT Quantum chemistry and DFT: approximations and equations From Schrödinger, HF and DFT to bases, SCF and correlation, including space groups, little-group irreps, SOC and time reversal in band calculations. Bilingual reading for 20 entries and 36 primary publications. Runnable validation covers two hydrogenic/He families and scoped finite-basis H₂ RHF. A fixed periodic-He LDA workflow is also available; general molecular DFT and other periodic materials remain unvalidated. Three choices to keep separate Physical model and approximation HF, KS-DFT, MP2, CI or CC: which many-electron states and energies are approximated? Representation and discretization Basis, grid, pseudopotential and k sampling: how is the model made finite? Equation solver Eigensolvers, SCF, mixing and DIIS: how accurately is the chosen discrete problem solved? SCF convergence, basis convergence and physical adequacy are distinct checks. Representative equations use atomic units (ℏ = m_e = e = 4πε₀ = 1). Finite molecules and periodic solids also require different boundaries. Schrodinger eigenproblems The common starting point is a many-electron eigenproblem at fixed nuclear positions. We use nonrelativistic Born–Oppenheimer theory and atomic units, separating electronic energy E_el from nuclear repulsion E_NN. R_A and Z_A denote nuclear positions and charges; r_ij is an electron–electron distance. For one electron the pair-repulsion sum vanishes; hydrogenic energies E_n = −Z²/(2n²) provide references. The many-electron wavefunction depends on all electronic coordinates and spins, unlike the individual three-dimensional orbitals in HF or KS. Uniform radial-grid tests of isolated hydrogenic 1s, 2s, 2p and 3d states; not a direct general many-electron Schrödinger solver. Fixed inputs, code and measured checks Separate fixed-input small-model release: Restricted fixed examples: Hydrogenic formulas and immutable finite-basis helium reference cards, Small 1D box and quantum harmonic-oscillator eigenpairs, A three-wave periodic projector and Fermi-occupation model. Saved-reference audits are not new electronic calculations. No new SCF, external-reference regeneration, complete-basis or correlated-exact helium claim. No separate certified finite-wall/mesh decomposition for HO; raw nodal count is a diagnostic. HO0.003 is the fixed-input study target, not a proved finite-h bound. The authored rank-one kernel is not an element-fitted norm-conserving pseudopotential. No self-consistent Hartree/XC, real metal, general material or long-time MD success. Hydrogenic formulas and immutable finite-basis helium reference cards Three saved 40-function He reference rows, hydrogenic analytic equations, p versus n and finite-grid/basis/model limits. Energies in hartree, radius in bohr; u in bohr^-1/2, p in bohr^-1 and n in bohr^-3. Three saved rows each use40basis functions, not40computed rows. No new SCF, external-reference regeneration, complete-basis or correlated-exact helium claim. Small 1D box and quantum harmonic-oscillator eigenpairs Finite Dirichlet boxes and central differences; whole-line HO formulas do not isolate finite-wall error. Node counts diagnostic until forward sign qualification. Atomic model units hbar=m=1 and HO omega=1. The box[0,1] and finite HO[-L,L] domains both use homogeneous Dirichlet conditions. No separate certified finite-wall/mesh decomposition for HO; raw nodal count is a diagnostic. HO0.003 is the fixed-input study target, not a proved finite-h bound. A three-wave periodic projector and Fermi-occupation model Authored rank-one periodic linear model and finite-N Helmholtz forces. No real metal/element pseudopotential/norm conservation/Hartree-XC/long MD claim. N=1.5 is a mean independent-particle Fermi occupation count, not an integer-N canonical many-body ensemble. Dimensionless G=-1,0,1,p=G+k,k=±.25 with equal.5weights,T=.05,mean electron countN=1.5 and spin factor2. No physical lattice-constant or metal mapping. The authored rank-one kernel is not an element-fitted norm-conserving pseudopotential. No self-consistent Hartree/XC, real metal, general material or long-time MD success. Nuclear dynamics, relativity, spin–orbit coupling and external fields are outside this representative Hamiltonian. A small eigenpair residual does not establish domain or basis convergence. Assumptions, implementation status and JSON Schrödinger, E. (1926) Roothaan, C. C. J. (1951) Hartree–Fock HF makes the energy stationary within single antisymmetric Slater determinants. Exchange follows from the determinant; electron correlation relative to the HF reference is absent. Closed-shell RHF builds its Fock operator from doubly occupied spatial orbitals. J_j is a Coulomb operator and K_j is generally nonlocal exchange. Open-shell choices include UHF and ROHF, with spin contamination and symmetry breaking requiring explicit diagnostics. Only spherical helium with one doubly occupied 1s spatial orbital; the local HF exchange reduction is specific to this two-electron problem. A separate edition adds H₂ RHF in finite s-Gaussian bases. Fixed inputs, code and measured checks New H₂ closed-shell RHF example: original s-Gaussian integrals, independent PySCF comparisons, SCF residuals and basis refinement. Limited to finite s-type subspaces; does not validate general molecules, molecular DFT, periodic systems or correct dissociation. Assumptions, implementation status and JSON Roothaan, C. C. J. (1951) Coulson, C. A.; Fischer, I. (1949) Kohn–Sham density functional theory / DFT Here DFT means density functional theory, rather than the discrete Fourier transform. note.en: Closed-shell occupied-orbital RHF equations include nonlocal exchange. Preserve existing He local-reduction and H2RHF examples. New calculations cover only fixed minimal two-electron H2/H3+ models; UHF equations have their own mapped model. No general multicenter molecules, global open-shell stability, complete-basis or general correlated-method guarantee.

Published examples cover spin-unpolarized exchange-only Dirac LDA for spherical helium and LDA exchange plus VWN5 correlation for fixed periodic He/He₂ cells. The radial atomic implementation and periodic PySCF workflows are separate series with different bases, boundaries and references. text.ja: 放射輸送・モーメント法 放射輸送では位置・方向・周波数に依存する強度を解きます。角度を積分したモーメント法は未知数を減らしますが、失われた角度情報を閉包で補う必要があります。 対象と代表式 ここでは静止媒質・周波数積分済みの灰色強度Iを考え、等方な放射源ηと吸収係数κを使い、散乱は省略します。κは長さの逆数です。E=(1/c)∫I dΩ、F=∫nI dΩ、P=(1/c)∫nnI dΩを定義すると、EとFの方程式はPを含みます。 1c∂tI+n⋅∇I=η−κI,∂tE+∇⋅F=4πη−cκE,c−2∂tF+∇⋅P=−κF/c. 計算の流れ 離散方向法は角度を直接離散化し、モーメント法はP=D EのEddingtonテンソルを閉じます。M1は局所E,FからDを与える代表例で、FLDはFをEの勾配から表す別の近似です。光学的厚い極限と自由流の極限を照合し、物質との交換を同じエネルギー収支で計算します。 適用条件と落とし穴 M1は異なる方向の交差ビームを一般には独立に運べません。FLDは勾配方向に流束を結び付けるため影や強い異方性に制約があります。縮約光速は物理的な伝播/緩和時間を変えるので、支配的な時間尺度との関係を明示します。 追加版も1次元定常・純吸収・指定流入の平板で、μ∂xI=−κIを解きます。一般の放射モーメント閉包、散乱、時間依存、多周波数や流体との結合は検証しません。 検証するときに見る量 吸収だけの指数減衰、等方拡散、自由流と影、交差ビームを分けて調べます。E≥0、|F|≤cEという実現可能性、放射と物質の総エネルギー、角度/空間/時間収束を確認します。閉包誤差と離散化誤差を混同しません。 Beer–Lambertの各ray解析解と連続角度の指数積分を使い、固定角度での風上空間誤差と、厳密ray伝播での角度求積誤差を分離します。流入−流出と体積吸収の収支・正値性を別に確認し、保存則だけで角度分布の精度を判定しません。 光学的厚さ0.1・0.7・3で、連続角度参照を指数積分expnと別の適応QUADPACK求積でも照合します。独立な輸送標本化では入射fluxに対応するμ=√Uを用い、透過をBernoulli変数として数えます。64反復の有限標本で二項信頼区間とRMSEを調べますが、公称95%の被覆を任意の入力や標本で保証したとは表示しません。 固定入力で確かめる：別々の配布版 各例の入力・観測量・診断の定義と適用範囲を確認します。検査の合格が示す内容は受入条件によって異なり、数学的な一般保証とは区別します。旧版の入力・測定・公差は保持します。 純吸収平板の離散座標放射輸送 固定した標的の計算例 純吸収の定常放射輸送を角度と空間で離散化し、Beer–Lambert解と積分された出射フラックスで検証します。 多重散乱、熱放射、周波数再分配、動的媒質、放射流体連成は未実装です。StamnesらのDISORTの全機能・安定化を再現したとは表示しません。 入力・結果・受入条件 · 手法・式・一次文献 · コード：run.py · コード：electrostatics.py · コード：fmm.py · コード：transport.py · テスト：test_particles.py · 配布ZIP · 保存結果 · 独立展開からの追試記録 放射輸送：空間・角度収束と光子統計 固定した標的の計算例 純吸収平板で特性解・独立適応求積・光子生存率を比較し、離散収支と標本誤差・区間被覆を別々に測ります。 区間被覆は有限の固定seedでの観測で、ちょうど95%の実測値や全seedの成功を保証しません。決定論的求積誤差を統計誤差へ含めず、多重散乱・周波数依存・熱放射・放射流体連成は未検証です。 text.en: Radiation transport and moment methods Radiation transport resolves intensity in space, direction and frequency. Moment methods reduce the angular dimension but require closure for information removed by integration. Problem and representative equations Use frequency-integrated grey intensity I in a static medium, with isotropic emissivity η and absorption coefficient κ of inverse-length units; omit scattering here. Define E=(1/c)∫I dΩ, F=∫nI dΩ and P=(1/c)∫nnI dΩ. Moment equations for E and F require a prescription for P. 1c∂tI+n⋅∇I=η−κI,∂tE+∇⋅F=4πη−cκE,c−2∂tF+∇⋅P=−κF/c. Algorithm Discrete ordinates discretizes angle directly; moment methods close P=D E. M1 obtains D locally from E and F, while flux-limited diffusion instead approximates F from the gradient of E. Check optically thick and free-streaming limits and couple matter exchange through a consistent energy balance. Conditions and pitfalls M1 generally cannot propagate crossing beams independently. FLD ties flux to the energy gradient, limiting shadows and strongly anisotropic fields. A reduced light speed changes transport/relaxation scales and must be justified against the physical time scales of interest. The companion retains a one-dimensional steady purely absorbing slab with specified inflow, solving μ∂xI=−κI. General radiation moment closures, scattering, time dependence, multiple frequencies and fluid coupling are unvalidated. What to check Test exponential absorption, isotropic diffusion, free streaming/shadows and crossing beams separately. Check E≥0, |F|≤cE, matter-plus-radiation energy and angular/spatial/time convergence. Distinguish closure error from discretization error. Use directional Beer–Lambert solutions and a continuum-angle exponential integral, separating upwind spatial error at fixed ordinates from angular-quadrature error with exact ray propagation. Check inflow–outflow versus volume absorption and positivity separately; a balance check alone does not establish angular-distribution accuracy. At optical depths 0.1/0.7/3, cross-check the continuum-angle reference using expn and a separate adaptive QUADPACK quadrature. Independent transport sampling draws μ=√U for the incident flux and counts transmission as a Bernoulli variable. Check binomial intervals and RMSE over 64 finite-sample replicates; nominal 95% coverage is not claimed for arbitrary inputs or samples. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Discrete-ordinate radiation transport through an absorbing slab Computation for a fixed target Discretize steady pure-absorption transfer in angle and space, checking Beer–Lambert rays and integrated exit flux. Multiple scattering, thermal emission, frequency redistribution, moving media and radiation–fluid coupling are unimplemented. This does not reproduce full DISORT functionality/stabilization. Input, results and acceptance · Method, equations and sources · Code: run.py · Code: electrostatics.py · Code: fmm.py · Code: transport.py · Tests: test_particles.py · Release ZIP · Saved results · Independent-extraction rerun receipt Radiation transport: space/angle convergence and photon statistics Computation for a fixed target Compare characteristics, independent adaptive integration and photon survival in a pure-absorption slab; separate discrete balance, sampling error and interval coverage. Coverage is observed over finite fixed seeds; neither exactly 95% empirical coverage nor all-seed success is guaranteed. Keep deterministic quadrature error separate from statistical error. Multiple scattering, frequency dependence, thermal emission and radiation hydrodynamics are unvalidated. Input, results and acceptance · Method, equations and sources · Code: run.py · Code: kinetic_experiments.py · Code: kinetics.py · Code: longrange_experiments.py · Code: electrostatics.py · Code: fmm.py · Tests: test_kinetics.py · Tests: test_longrange.py · Tests: test_runner.py · Release ZIP · Saved results · Independent-extraction rerun receipt Publication scope and related entries The historical reading, equations, sources and release are preserved; a separate companion release supplies bounded checks for fixed conditions. This does not mean every general verification suggestion above has been executed. Consult each release’s dedicated page and saved record for inputs, references, checks and limits. Bibliographic verification differs from consulting selected passages; neither implies a full-paper audit or numerical reproduction. Access-depth notes accompany each source. C.D. Levermore (1984).
